The platform covers player authentication across Steam, Epic Games, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, Apple, Google, and custom white-label flows, as well as leaderboards, player progressions, virtual economies, persistent storage, cloud saves, and player file hosting. Developers can also access character systems, asset management, in-app purchasing, missions, collectibles, and Twitch Drops integration through a unified API surface. SDKs are available for Unity, Unreal Engine, and Godot, with basic integration support for GameMaker, Construct 3, and GDevelop.

providers.name: Roblox
providers.description: Roblox is a user-generated content platform where creators build, publish, and monetize immersive 3D experiences using Roblox Studio and the Luau scripting language. Roblox exposes three distinct developer surfaces: the in-engine Luau scripting API (Roblox Engine API) running inside experiences and Studio plugins, the Roblox Studio plugin API for editor tooling, and the Open Cloud API (apis.roblox.com) for external programmatic access from servers, build pipelines, and back-office tools. The Open Cloud surface covers DataStores, Memory Stores, Messaging Service, Place Publishing, Universes, Assets, Inventory, Users, Groups, Notifications, Subscriptions, and Luau Execution, authenticated either with API keys scoped per-resource or with OAuth 2.0 for third-party apps. Roblox also publishes deep documentation for the Engine API at create.roblox.com/docs and the legacy ROBLOX Web APIs that power the website (subdomains such as users.roblox.com, groups.roblox.com, inventory.roblox.com), which remain undocumented for third parties.

providers.name: The Promenade
providers.description: The Promenade (The Promenade Studios) is a San Francisco AI studio, backed by a16z, that builds Simcluster (simcluster.ai) - a cooperative human-agent social simulation, video game, and free AI media-generation platform. Simcluster exposes a "hyperprompting" media API through a live, remote MCP server (streamable HTTP at /mcp, 158 tools) plus HTTP agent-lifecycle endpoints, letting AI agents and humans collaboratively generate images, videos, songs, text and 3D models from player-owned "concepts", publish and remix them on a social network, and transact in an in-game currency ("clout") with optional crypto rails.

providers.name: Niantic
providers.description: Niantic Spatial, Inc. (spun out of Niantic, Inc. in 2025 after the sale of its games division to Scopely) builds real-world foundation models for physical AI. Its Large Geospatial Model (LGM), trained on 30+ billion posed real-world images, powers a three-part geospatial platform — Reconstruct (3D models via Gaussian splats and meshes), Localize (VPS, centimeter-level 6DoF visual positioning that works indoors, outdoors, and in GPS-denied environments), and Understand (semantic querying of 3D maps). Developers build on the Niantic Spatial Development Kit (NSDK 4.x, formerly the Lightship ARDK) across Unity, Swift, Android, and ROS 2, connecting to Scaniverse and VPS 2.0. Enterprise focus areas include robotics, defense and intelligence, and oil and gas.

providers.name: SideQuest
providers.description: SideQuest is a VR content-discovery platform and independent app store for Meta Quest, PCVR, Pico, Magic Leap and WebXR headsets — the home of sideload-only, early-access and indie VR apps and games, plus tools to help users get more from their VR headset. SideQuest operates a public REST API (api.sidequestvr.com) for browsing the app catalog and reading user profiles and achievements, secured with OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens and a device-style short-code login. Backed by GV.

providers.name: Autodesk Maya
providers.description: Autodesk Maya is a comprehensive 3D computer graphics application used for creating interactive 3D applications including video games, animated films, TV series, and visual effects. Maya provides multiple programming APIs including a Python API, C++ plugin API, MEL scripting language, USD integration, and Bifrost visual programming environment for extending and automating Maya workflows and creating custom tools and plugins.

providers.name: Smashgg
providers.description: Smashgg (now start.gg, following its acquisition by Microsoft) is a competitive-gaming and esports platform for running tournaments, brackets, and leagues across fighting games and other titles. Its public developer API is a single GraphQL endpoint (https://api.start.gg/gql/alpha) exposing tournaments, events, entrants, sets, phases, standings, players, and users, plus mutations for reporting set results and managing seeding and brackets. Authentication is via personal access tokens (Bearer, 1-year expiry) or OAuth 2.0 authorization-code tokens scoped to a user. The original smash.gg domain now redirects to start.gg.

providers.name: LIV
providers.description: LIV is an XR video capture and live-streaming platform whose flagship product, the LIV Camera Kit (LCK), is a game-engine SDK for Unity and Unreal Engine. It lets extended-reality apps on Meta Quest and PCVR embed user-spawnable in-game cameras for recording video, capturing screenshots, and live streaming to YouTube, Twitch, and custom RTMP endpoints - with no external capture hardware or software. An official Meta Quest partner, LIV ships first-party Unity and Unreal SDKs, a Developer Dashboard for SDK downloads and Tracking IDs, a LIV Hub device-login flow for streaming and subscriptions, and a desktop LIV App URI/command API for mixed-reality capture. The SDK is free for developers and is used by apps serving millions of monthly active users.

bands.label: Emerging
bands.blurb: More than an index entry but still mostly links rather than artifacts.

providers.name: FRVR
providers.description: FRVR is a gaming company that builds and distributes instant, no-download HTML5 games across channels beyond the app stores — Facebook Instant, Google Play, iOS WebView, Samsung, Xiaomi, and web portals. Its developer surface is the FRVR SDK: a single JavaScript SDK (with thin wrappers for Unity WebGL exports, Cocos Creator, and Construct 3) that integrates ads, in-app purchases, analytics, auth, local and cloud storage, social/friends, leaderboards, tournaments, challenges, consent, and notifications into a game, then adapts per distribution channel while FRVR's release pipeline injects the correct channel bundle at build time. FRVR also operates the UpIt no-code game creation tool. Backed by Accel.

providers.name: Series AI
providers.description: Series AI (Series Entertainment, Inc.) is an a16z-backed, AI-native game company behind RUN.world, a platform to create, publish, play, and monetize HTML5 games. Series ships a real first-party developer surface: the RUN.world SDK (@series-inc/rundot-game-sdk) exposes a single RundotGameAPI for player storage, profiles, leaderboards, ad monetization, purchases, entitlements, multiplayer, server-authoritative simulation, and generative AI (image, audio, video, and text), while the rundot CLI scaffolds, deploys, versions, and operates live titles. StowKit asset tooling, a Three.js-based 3D engine with ECS, the Syncplay deterministic-multiplayer core, and a community workshop of game starters round out the toolchain. Founded by veterans from Riot, Epic, Blizzard, Pocket Gems, and Telltale.

providers.name: SayDuck
providers.description: Sayduck is a 3D product visualization platform for ecommerce that turns static product pages into interactive shopping experiences. Brands upload 3D assets to a self-service platform and embed them as interactive 3D configurators, WebAR (view-in-your-space) experiences, and virtual product photography. The public integration surface is a browser-native Web Component (`<sayduck-viewer>`) with an in-page JavaScript API driven by DOM CustomEvents; the platform is backed by a GraphQL API internally. Founded in 2012 by Niklas Slotte, part of Goodbye Kansas Group 2019-2023, and independent since 2024 via The Optical Foundry.

providers.name: Limit Break
providers.description: Limit Break Inc. is a gaming and onchain-economy company that builds the Apptoken protocol suite — a family of permissionlessly deployable EVM smart contract protocols for programmable digital economies. Its Creator Token Standards (ERC-20C, ERC-721C, ERC-1155C) route every transfer through an on-chain Transfer Validator so creators can bind modular rulesets, operator whitelists and blacklists without changing their token contract. Around that foundation Limit Break ships Payment Processor for royalty-enforced NFT trading, TokenMaster for backed fungible tokens with pool-based buy/sell/spend flows, the Limit Break AMM with a multi-tier hook system, PermitC for time-bound token approvals, Wrapped Native as a gas-efficient WETH9 replacement, and Trusted Forwarder for application attribution. Integration is documented at apptokens.com, distributed as Solidity via Foundry and npm, and supported by 25 first-party AI agent skills. Limit Break is backed by Paradigm.

providers.name: String Technology Inc
providers.description: String (string.xyz) is a fiat interoperability platform for Web3 gaming, operated by String Technology Inc and backed by 500 Global. String lets game developers accept credit-card and bank payments natively inside their games, acting as the merchant of record and counterparty for fiat on/off ramps, NFT purchases, and cross-chain payments. A player pays fiat on traditional rails and String delivers the digital asset on-chain — either by interacting with the game's smart contract to mint/send an NFT or by sending a token from its treasury to the player's wallet. String ships three integration surfaces — String Checkout (drop-in payment app), a Unity SDK, and String Direct (custom web SDK) — all wrapping a REST API at string-api.xyz that covers API keys, contracts, platforms (games), members, organizations, users (players), saved cards, wallet-signature login, quotes, and transactions.

providers.name: Bezi
providers.description: Bezi is an AI agent for Unity game developers that runs directly inside the Unity Editor. It indexes a project's scripts, assets, scenes, packages and documentation in real time to deliver context-aware debugging, code generation, shader creation, scene building and no-code Unity tool automation that follows each project's own conventions. Bezi supports multiple frontier models (Claude Sonnet, GPT, GLM and others), a Skills system for packaging repeatable workflows, MCP connections for external context (Blender, Miro, Notion, Perforce and more), and real-time collaborative team workspaces. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Uncork Capital. Bezi ships an in-editor product and desktop/plugin experience rather than a public HTTP API.

providers.name: Genies
providers.description: Genies is an AI avatar and digital-identity company that powers the visual and embodiment layer for AI. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in West Hollywood / Venice, California, Genies builds high-fidelity, fully customizable 3D avatars and "Smart Avatars" — LLM- and behavior-driven digital characters that can act, react, converse, and persist across games, apps, and XR experiences. For developers, Genies ships a Unity-based Avatar SDK (C#) with avatar loading, a customization API for wearables/hair/makeup/tattoos, and asset pre-caching, supporting iOS, Android, Windows Standalone, and VR. Developers register a project in the Genies Developer Hub to obtain API keys used by the SDK. Backed by Bond Capital, Multicoin Capital, and Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: Godot Engine
providers.description: Godot Engine is a free and open-source community-driven 2D and 3D game engine released under the MIT License and stewarded by the Godot Foundation. Godot ships an integrated editor plus a deep scripting and extension surface across three primary languages: GDScript (Godot's own typed scripting language), C# (via .NET 8 / Mono in the .NET build), and C++ (via GDExtension, the modern successor to GDNative, which lets native shared libraries register their own classes against the same API the built-in classes use). The engine API is documented per-class at docs.godotengine.org. In addition, the Godot Asset Library at godotengine.org/asset-library/api exposes a public REST API used by the in-editor AssetLib browser to list, search, fetch, and download community plugins, templates, tools, and demos. The Godot project source lives at github.com/godotengine/godot.

providers.name: W4 Games
providers.description: W4 Games is the company commercializing the open-source Godot game engine. It provides hands-on professional services (adoption, architecture, performance, production readiness), advanced console ports and mobile/XR platform work, and premium enterprise support for studios shipping with Godot. Its developer product is W4 Cloud (W4GD) — a managed multiplayer backend-as-a-service for Godot covering player authentication, a Supabase/PostgREST database accessed through the W4 Relational Mapper (W4RM) ORM, realtime, storage, matchmaking and lobbies, WebRTC, analytics, and Agones-based dedicated game-server fleets. W4 Cloud is consumed through the w4gd Godot editor addon (GDScript SDK) rather than a standalone public REST API. Backed by Lux Capital.

providers.name: Microsoft Xbox
providers.description: APIs for Xbox gaming platform including Xbox Live Services and Azure PlayFab backend for games.

providers.name: Triumph
providers.description: Triumph (Triumph Labs, formerly Triumph Arcade) is a consumer entertainment and commerce company backed by General Catalyst, which led its $10.2M Series A — part of the $14.1M the company launched with in May 2023. Triumph began as an iOS/Unity SDK that let game developers add real-money tournaments to their games, handling payments, state-by-state regulatory eligibility (37 US states plus DC at launch), matchmaking, and payouts, and today operates two consumer apps: Triumph: Play for Cash (competitive cash gaming arcade) and Rips by Triumph (trading-card collectibles). The Triumph SDK for Swift and Unity remains documented at docs.triumpharcade.com and is distributed via CocoaPods and GitHub, with a developer dashboard at dashboard.triumpharcade.com; the company publishes no public REST API.

providers.name: Freeverse
providers.description: Freeverse is the team behind the LAOS Network, an EVM-compatible Polkadot parachain and public blockchain protocol for Bridgeless Minting and Evolution of digital assets (NFTs). Rather than bridging tokens between chains, LAOS lets applications mint and dynamically evolve NFTs whose ownership is enforced on established chains such as Ethereum and Polygon while the asset logic and gas costs live on LAOS. The LAOS Foundation maintains a public GraphQL API at api.laosnetwork.io that lets developers create collections, mint up to 700 NFTs in a single atomic operation, evolve existing assets, broadcast assets to marketplaces, and run read queries over an on-chain indexer. Read queries are open; write mutations require an API key. Freeverse originated as a Barcelona blockchain gaming and digital-ownership company (Living Assets, Crypto-soccer) and is a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital.

providers.name: GDevelop
providers.description: GDevelop is an open-source, no-code, cross-platform 2D/3D and multiplayer game engine designed for everyone. Creators build games visually with a drag-and-drop event system (with optional JavaScript to extend behavior) and export in one click to web browsers, Android, iOS, Steam, and desktop. GDevelop offers a web editor and a downloadable desktop app, an asset store, cloud project storage, leaderboards, and multiplayer features, and is developed in the open on GitHub (4ian/GDevelop). It ships with a documented JavaScript runtime (GDJS), an extensive wiki, and a games platform for publishing and monetizing creations. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Seedcamp portfolio company and enriched via the pipeline.

providers.name: Snapser
providers.description: Snapser is a plug-and-play, modular backend-as-a-service platform for game studios and app developers. Instead of building infrastructure from scratch, teams assemble a backend from modular "Snaps" — managed microservices such as Authentication, Profiles, Storage, Leaderboards, Inventory, Chat, Social Graph, Matchmaking, Analytics, and an Event Bus — and deploy them together as a "Snapend" cluster fronted by its own API gateway. Developers can bring their own custom code (BYOSnap), game servers (BYOGS), and local workstations (BYOWS), then generate typed client SDKs and gRPC protobufs for a wide range of engines and languages including Unity, Unreal, Godot, Cocos, Roblox, iOS, Android, Flutter, C#, C++, Go, Python, TypeScript, Rust, and more. The snapctl CLI drives the entire build-and-deploy workflow. Snapser is backed by a16z.

providers.name: Overwolf
providers.description: Overwolf enables developers to build lightweight in-game applications and overlays using HTML and JavaScript. The platform provides APIs for game events, game data, and in-game overlay functionality.

providers.name: Abios (Sportradar)
providers.description: Abios, a Sportradar company headquartered in Stockholm, provides enterprise-scale esports data, odds, and engagement products for sportsbooks and media platforms. The Abios Atlas API delivers REST and WebSocket access to fixtures, live statistics, odds, and player props across 60,000+ yearly matches and 50 billion+ data points spanning major esports titles plus traditional sports coverage via Sportradar integration.

providers.name: Sony
providers.description: Sony Group Corporation is a Japanese multinational spanning electronics, gaming, entertainment, image sensors, and financial services. Sony's developer-facing surface includes the Neural Network Libraries (NNabla) deep-learning framework, the Spresense IoT board SDK, Sonyflake distributed ID service, and a portfolio of Go and embedded-Linux open-source tooling maintained on github.com/Sony.

providers.name: Leap Motion
providers.description: Leap Motion is the hand-tracking company behind the Leap Motion Controller. It merged with Ultrahaptics in 2019 to form Ultraleap, and the Leap Motion brand now continues as Ultraleap's hardware line (Leap Motion Controller 2) and as the "Leap" naming across the tracking SDK. The developer surface is not a hosted web API: it is LeapC, a native C API that connects a local client to the Ultraleap Hand Tracking Service and delivers tracked hands, digits, bones, images and device events as polled messages, plus first-party plugins for Unity, Unreal, OpenXR and Python. The original leapmotion.com and developer.leapmotion.com domains no longer resolve; docs.ultraleap.com and github.com/ultraleap are the live developer surfaces.

providers.name: Rive
providers.description: Rive is an interactive design and animation platform and real-time graphics engine that lets designers, animators, and developers create, animate, and code interactive experiences in one place and ship them across every platform. Built around a State Machine design system and a GPU-accelerated vector renderer that draws at up to 120fps, Rive exports a single lightweight .riv file that is driven at runtime by open-source (MIT) native runtimes for Web, React, React Native, Flutter, iOS, Android, macOS, Unity, Unreal, and C++. Rive powers interactive UI, animation, and product experiences at companies including Spotify, Duolingo, Disney, and Google, reaching over 2 billion users. Rather than a hosted REST API, Rive's developer surface is its family of first-party runtime SDKs plus data binding, Luau scripting, and a CDN for share and embed hosting.

providers.name: Varjo
providers.description: Varjo is a Helsinki-based maker of high-fidelity virtual and mixed reality headsets for professional training and simulation across air, land, and sea. Its platform centers on the XR-4 Series headsets and the Varjo Base companion software, with a developer surface built around a native C SDK (rendering, foveated rendering, mixed reality, eye and hand tracking, DataStream API), the Varjo XR Plugin for Unity, an OpenXR plugin for Unreal Engine, and WebXR support. Varjo ships its own Khronos OpenXR runtime and is a contributing member of the OpenXR working group.

providers.name: BreederDAO
providers.description: BreederDAO (rebranded as Sovrun) is a Web3 gaming infrastructure company that began as a factory for high-volume, in-game NFT assets — breeding and crafting digital items for blockchain games and gaming guilds — and has since evolved into a platform for fully on-chain games and Autonomous Worlds. Its developer surface today centers on the Sovrun SDK (traditional game-dev tooling stitched to on-chain game and Autonomous World generators), the Chain Tactics moddable game, the $SOVRN token running on EVM chains (Ethereum, Base, and a Hyperliquid-based Sovrun L2), and the ReadyGamer API — a joint venture with Virtuals that exposes an HTTP endpoint for AI-agent NPC chat inside games such as Roblox. Backed by a16z.

providers.name: High Fidelity
providers.description: High Fidelity provides live spatial audio technology for apps and games. Its Spatial Audio Client Library (hifi-spatial-audio, MIT) lets developers embed realistic positional voice — 3D azimuth/distance transforms, nearfield "whisper" audio, noise reduction, and many simultaneous speakers over the Opus codec — into web and native applications, and previously connected them to a hosted Spatial Audio API server via signed connection JWTs. Apps including Clubhouse, Hubbub, Breakroom, and Soundstage used the technology. The hosted API service has since been discontinued; the SDK remains open source, and the company's active product is Quad, a spatial social platform that recreates physical meeting spaces. High Fidelity was founded by Philip Rosedale and is a portfolio company of GV.

providers.name: AI Arena
providers.description: AI Arena is a web3/AI gaming company built by ArenaX Labs, backed by Paradigm and Framework Ventures. Its flagship title, AI Arena, is an Ethereum/Arbitrum-native PvP fighting game where players purchase, train through imitation learning, and battle characters powered by real artificial intelligence, with a native $NRN (Neuron) token and an on-chain marketplace for AI models. Beyond the game, ArenaX Labs ships developer infrastructure for reinforcement learning: RLMesh, an open-source, Gymnasium-compatible framework that connects RL models to environments across process, dependency, and machine boundaries over a gRPC wire protocol (rlmesh-wire-v1), with Python and Rust SDKs; and SAI (competesai.com), a gamified RL research and competition platform with its own CLI. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from public sources — GitHub, package registries, and the RLMesh documentation.

providers.name: Spline
providers.description: Spline is a real-time collaborative 3D design tool with AI-driven object generation, web embedding, and animation. Spline does NOT publish a REST API for 3D scene generation as of May 2026; instead it exposes Code APIs (Web, SwiftUI, Kotlin) for embedding scenes, plus a real-time API for variables/data and webhooks for event-driven integrations.

providers.name: TheMonetizr
providers.description: Monetizr (TheMonetizr) is a gaming media platform for in-game brand advertising that turns gameplay into measurable, voluntary, and non-skippable brand engagement. Brands run branded campaigns and missions inside mobile games; players complete them for in-game or brand-sponsored rewards, reporting >30% average engagement, >90% viewability, and >85% video completion across a 340M mobile-gamer reach. The Monetizr Campaigns API (base https://api.themonetizr.com) serves active campaigns to games — listing campaigns/missions, resetting progress, and claiming rewards — and is consumed by the official open-source Unity SDK using a per-game HTTP Bearer API key. The company is a Techstars-backed portfolio company.

providers.name: Unreal Engine
providers.description: Unreal Engine is Epic Games' real-time 3D engine for games, film, broadcast, architecture, simulation, automotive, and live events. The engine is shipped as a downloadable editor, source on GitHub (under the Unreal Engine EULA), and a deep C++ and Blueprint API surface rather than a public REST API. The developer-facing surface includes the Unreal C++ API reference, the Blueprint visual scripting API, the Online Subsystem (OSS) abstraction over platform backends, the Pixel Streaming framework for streaming Unreal apps over WebRTC, the Render Hardware Interface (RHI), the Slate UI framework, and a plugin and Marketplace ecosystem (now Fab). Programmatic backend integration for Unreal-built games is typically delivered via Epic Online Services (EOS), profiled separately. This profile documents Unreal Engine as an SDK and tooling surface rather than as a REST API.

providers.name: Nexon Inc
providers.description: Nexon (operated by Nexon Korea Co., Ltd.) is a global video game publisher whose NEXON Open API platform at openapi.nexon.com gives developers programmatic access to per-game data such as character, ranking, and match information. Requests are authenticated with a per-application API key sent in the x-nxopen-api-key HTTP header and served from open.api.nexon.com; the developer portal provides application registration, usage analytics, per-game API references, and integration guides.

providers.name: CleverPet
providers.description: CleverPet is a pet-technology company behind the CleverPet Hub, a programmable "game console for pets" that gives dogs and cats mental stimulation through puzzle games and dispenses food treats as rewards. The Hub is built on the Particle IoT platform, and CleverPet publishes hackerpet, an open-source Particle/Arduino C++ library that lets developers write, customize, and share their own games by controlling the Hub's lights, food pod, and tray motor through the HubInterface class. The company was part of the Techstars accelerator, and its team and open-source hardware/software work continued under the FluentPet brand.

providers.name: Metacritic
providers.description: Metacritic is a review aggregator that collects critic and user scores for games, movies, TV shows, and music, computing a weighted Metascore for each title. The Metacritic API (provided via Fabric Origin / IVA / Gracenote) gives programmatic access to Metascores, user scores, individual critic reviews, publication details, and entertainment rankings for movies and television. Unofficial community-built wrappers also expose game, movie, and TV data from Metacritic's public backend.

providers.name: Xiao-Y Technology (小y科技)
providers.description: Xiao-Y Technology (小y科技), operated by Beijing Shiyou Interactive Technology Co., Ltd. (北京视游互动科技有限公司), is a Chinese smart-TV and big-screen gaming platform behind the 小y游戏厅 TV game store and YFans app, publishing licensed TV editions of titles like 葫芦娃, 胡莱三国2, 我叫MT2, and 中超荣耀. Its 小y手游开放平台 developer platform onboards game studios through first-party YTS SDKs (Android Fusion and iOS) rather than a public REST API, covering registration, qualification review, game submission, and revenue sharing. A Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company.

providers.name: Tripo3D
providers.description: Tripo3D (by VAST) is an AI 3D generation platform with text-to-3D, image-to-3D, mesh refinement, and texturing APIs producing game-ready 3D assets. The Tripo API uses an async task-based REST pattern at https://api.tripo3d.ai/v2/openapi/task. Authenticate with API key.

providers.name: Forte Labs
providers.description: Forte builds on-chain compliance and economic tooling for games and Web3 applications. Its flagship developer product, the Forte Rules Engine, is an open-source EVM protocol that lets developers define powerful, flexible, and composable on-chain policies — for regulatory compliance, risk management, and token-economy design — without hardcoding rules into their smart contracts. The engine centers on policies, rules, trackers, and calling/foreign contracts, ships client contracts for the ERC20/721/1155/721A token standards, and is consumed through a TypeScript SDK. Forte was founded in 2019 and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Battery Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners, and Canaan. This profile catalogs Forte's public developer surface — Rules Engine documentation, SDK, and GitHub organization.

providers.name: KaBum!
providers.description: KaBuM! is the largest e-commerce retailer of technology, computer hardware, electronics, and games in Latin America, headquartered in Limeira, Brazil and part of the Magalu (Magazine Luiza) group. Beyond its consumer storefront, KaBuM! operates a third-party seller marketplace on the Mirakl platform and publishes an integration guide for sellers and integrators to connect their ERP/OMS to the marketplace via a REST API — managing product catalog, attribute mapping, offers (price/stock), order retrieval, shipping carriers, document uploads, and tracking/ship confirmation. Authentication is API-key based, write operations are expected to be idempotent, and integrations poll asynchronous import jobs by id. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio lead and enriched from KaBuM!'s public integration documentation.

providers.name: Scenario
providers.description: Scenario is a Paris- and San Francisco-headquartered AI platform for game asset generation founded in 2021 by Emmanuel de Maistre and Hervé Nivon. The Scenario REST API lets game studios and creative teams generate consistent, on-brand images, video, audio, and 3D assets, train custom LoRA models on their own reference art, automate batch asset pipelines, and integrate AI-generated visuals into production tools like Unity. Scenario aggregates 500+ AI models from 50+ providers behind a single workspace and API, with full commercial licensing for generated assets and enterprise SSO, SOC 2 Type II, and governance controls.

providers.name: Looking Glass Factory
providers.description: Looking Glass Factory builds group-viewable 3D holographic (light field) displays that require no headset — the Looking Glass Go, Portrait, and the 16", 27", 32", 65" and 86" Light Field and Hololuminescent displays. Beyond hardware it ships a real developer surface: the Looking Glass Bridge runtime exposes a local HTTP REST API for driving the on-device media player, the hosted Blocks GraphQL API at blocks.glass lets apps upload and share holograms (quilt and RGBD images/videos), and official SDKs cover JavaScript/TypeScript (bridge.js, blocks.js, WebXR), Python (Bridge Python SDK), C/C++/C# (Core SDK), plus Unity and Unreal Engine plugins. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Foundry Group and enriched from its public developer documentation, GitHub org, and package registries.

providers.name: Mythical Games
providers.description: Mythical Games is a Web3 game-technology studio and platform company (an a16z portfolio company) that builds games with player-owned digital items and a secondary marketplace economy. Its business has two sides: consumer game titles (FIFA Rivals, Pudgy Party, Blankos) and the Mythical Platform, a B2B toolkit that lets any game add a secondary economy of tradeable items and currencies. The platform is exposed to integrating studios primarily through gRPC/Protobuf SDKs — the Saga SDK and the earlier IVI SDK — published for Java, C++, and Python, rather than a public REST/OpenAPI surface. The Saga gRPC API covers items, item types, currencies, currency types, listings, offers, player wallets, reservations, an NFT bridge, and metadata, with cursor-based queries and a server-streaming status channel for confirming asynchronous writes. Assets settle on the Mythos chain, a Polkadot/Substrate gaming parachain (MYTH token) whose node software is open source.

providers.name: Didimo
providers.description: Didimo is a digital human and 3D character technology company whose flagship product, Popul8, automates the creation of game-ready NPCs, crowds, and digital humans at scale. Popul8 Express lets studios generate thousands of fully-rigged, high-quality characters from a single 3D base template, with automated asset fitting, shape and rig transfer, intersection solving, material and deformable variation, and crowd rendering optimized for Unity and Unreal Engine. Beyond the desktop application, Popul8 ships a headless command-line tool (Popul8 CLI) for automating crowd-generation pipelines in CI/CD, plus Unity and Unreal bridges for bringing characters and crowds directly into game engines. Didimo is headquartered in Clearwater, Florida with offices in Portugal and the UK, and was backed by Techstars.

providers.name: KGeN
providers.description: KGeN (Kratos Gamer Network) is a verified-human data network powering Physical AI and Large Language Models across the Global South, and the operator of the KGeN Economy Protocols — a suite of developer APIs (Esports and Loyalty) that let game studios add leaderboard-based competitions and customizable reward systems paid in KCash, redeemable for real-world items at the Kratos Store. Server-to-server and per-user (JWT/OTP) endpoints cover sessions, tournaments, wallets, rewards, and rewardable events. Company revenue feeds $KGEN tokenomics, where every AI-data contract permanently retires token supply on-chain. Backed by Accel and Prosus Ventures.

providers.name: Ronin Network
providers.description: Ronin is an Ethereum sidechain originally built by Sky Mavis to power Axie Infinity and a wider game and NFT economy. The network exposes a standard Ethereum-style JSON-RPC interface on mainnet and the Saigon testnet, the Ronin Explorer, a canonical bridge to Ethereum, and the Skynet Web3 data API for indexed accounts, NFTs, contracts, and transactions. Sky Mavis layers on game and platform APIs (Axie Infinity Origins, AXP, Ronin Market Partner, Ronin Store, Account, Wallet, Gas Sponsoring, Katana Swap) administered through the Ronin Developer Console.

providers.name: Tripo AI
providers.description: Tripo AI (VAST AI Research) is an AI 3D content platform that converts text, images, and multi-view photographs into production-ready 3D assets. The platform exposes a REST API at api.tripo3d.ai that orchestrates a unified "task" abstraction across text-to-3D, image-to-3D, multi-view-to-3D, AI texturing, mesh segmentation, model refinement, stylization, format conversion, automatic rigging, retargeting, and one-shot animation. An official Python SDK, an MCP server, and engine plugins for Blender, Unity, Unreal Engine, ComfyUI, Cocos, and Godot wrap the API for creative and game pipelines. Open-source research artifacts (TripoSR, TripoSG, UniRig) ship separately on GitHub under the VAST-AI-Research organization.

providers.name: Homa Games
providers.description: Homa Games is a global mobile game developer and publisher headquartered in Paris, France, and backed by Northzone. Through its Homa Lab platform the company pairs data-driven tooling with creative expertise to help studios build commercially successful hyper-casual and hybrid-casual games, having worked with more than 1,000 studios to ship 80+ titles that have surpassed one billion downloads. Its developer surface centers on the Homa SDK (Homa Belly), a no-code Unity meta-SDK that bundles user consent, analytics, ad mediation, attribution and A/B ("N-testing") tooling, alongside Homa Lab modules for market watching, ideation, creative testing, analytics and the Homa Academy. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Northzone portfolio company and enriched here with its published developer-surface link properties and a domain-security profile; Homa exposes an SDK and developer platform rather than a public REST API.

providers.name: Common Sense Machines
providers.description: Common Sense Machines (CSM) builds 3D world models with image-to-3D and 3D world simulation APIs aimed at games, robotics, and synthetic data. The CSM Cube product family released a single-click model pipeline with mesh-parts-based topology in early 2026. API access is bundled with mid-tier and enterprise CSM subscription plans.

providers.name: Klang Games
providers.description: Klang Games is an entertainment and game development studio headquartered in Berlin, founded in 2013 by three Icelandic co-founders — Mundi Vondi (CEO), Oddur Snær Magnússon (CTO) and Ívar Emilsson (CCO) — several of whom came out of CCP and EVE Online. Its flagship product is SEED, a persistent large-scale MMO society simulator built on Google Cloud, backed by investors including Animoca Brands, Supercell, LEGO Ventures, Anthos Capital, Kingway Capital and Northzone. Klang publishes no developer platform: there is no API documentation, no SDKs and no partner program. The only publicly discoverable machine interface is the OpenID Connect provider behind SEED player accounts, captured in this repo from its discovery documents.

providers.name: HowLongToBeat
providers.description: HowLongToBeat is a game completion time database that tracks how long it takes to finish thousands of video games. Community-sourced data provides average completion times across multiple play styles including main story, main story plus extras, completionist, and all styles. The site is owned by IGN Entertainment (Ziff Davis) and does not publish an official public API; all programmatic access relies on community-built wrappers that query the website directly.

providers.name: SOUNDRAW
providers.description: SOUNDRAW is an AI music generation platform that produces royalty-free, copyright-cleared music customized by genre, mood, theme, length, and instrumentation. Beyond the soundraw.io consumer product, SOUNDRAW offers a B2B API for embedding music generation into video platforms, games, social tools, and ad tech, with Canva, Filmora, and Captions Mirage cited as integration partners.

providers.name: Babylon.js
providers.description: Babylon.js is an Apache-2.0 licensed, TypeScript-first open-source 3D engine and rendering framework sponsored by Microsoft and developed in the public BabylonJS GitHub organization. It targets WebGL, WebGPU, and WebXR in the browser, and DirectX, Metal, Vulkan, OpenGL, and OpenGL ES natively through Babylon Native — including a Babylon React Native binding for mobile. The framework ships as a family of scoped npm packages (`@babylonjs/core`, `gui`, `loaders`, `materials`, `inspector`, `serializers`, `post-processes`, `procedural-textures`, `node-editor`) plus a rich tooling surface — the Playground IDE, Sandbox asset viewer, Inspector, Spector.js, the Node Material / Geometry / Particle / Render-Graph editors, a community Editor, the Babylon Toolkit (Unity / Unreal exporters), and DCC exporters for 3ds Max, Maya, and Blender — all backed by the public Snippet API at `snippet.babylonjs.com` that powers shareable Playground and node-editor assets.

providers.name: Faraway
providers.description: Faraway is a web3 gaming company building an interoperable gaming ecosystem for players, creators, and studios. Its platform lets game studios integrate player-driven, blockchain-based economies into their titles across EVM-compatible chains and Solana, with a unified player identity and wallet (id.faraway.com), a creator platform for user-generated content and monetization (create.faraway.com), and an in-game marketplace and secondary-trading shop (shop.faraway.com). Faraway publishes a developer platform with an API reference and an llms.txt index at docs.faraway.com. The company is backed by a16z, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Open 3D Foundation
providers.description: The Open 3D Foundation is a Linux Foundation project supporting the Open 3D Engine (O3DE), an open source, real-time 3D engine for building games, simulations, and other 3D applications. With Microsoft as a premier member, it provides a modular, cross-platform engine with advanced rendering capabilities.

providers.name: Forte
providers.description: Forte is a Web3 economic infrastructure company building compliance and economic tools for games and digital-asset economies. Its flagship product is the Forte Rules Engine, a free, open-source, EVM-compatible on-chain policy engine that lets smart-contract developers define composable, adaptive rules (KYC gates, OFAC/sanctions screening, vesting schedules, circuit breakers, and other economic guardrails) without hardcoding logic into their contracts. The Rules Engine ships a TypeScript SDK and Solidity client contracts, and is complemented by a ZK Policy Engine for privacy-preserving policy enforcement. Forte is backed by a16z, Canaan Partners, and Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: Audiomob
providers.description: Audiomob is an in-game and in-app audio advertising platform that lets mobile game and app publishers monetize their titles with non-interruptive, skippable and rewarded audio ads while advertisers reach engaged gaming audiences at scale. Publishers integrate through the Audiomob Unity plugin or native iOS and Android SDKs (plus a community React Native adapter), add their games to the Audiomob developer dashboard, and configure ad units, an Ad Availability API, and server-to-server webhooks for reward and event tracking. The platform is Open Measurement (IAB Tech Lab) compliant, supports consent management via OneTrust and Sourcepoint, exposes Impression Level Revenue Data (ILRD), and integrates with mediation partners such as AdMob and LevelPlay (MAX) and mobile measurement partners including Adjust, Singular and Tenjin. The current SDK line is SDK 10. Audiomob is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Magic Leap
providers.description: Magic Leap is an augmented reality company headquartered in Plantation, Florida, building see-through AR optics (waveguides and display systems) and the Magic Leap 2 enterprise AR headset, along with a developer platform for spatial computing. Developers build on-device applications using the Magic Leap Unity SDK, an OpenXR runtime, and a native C API, distributed through the Magic Leap Hub package registry and the company's GitHub organization. Magic Leap does not publish a public hosted REST API or OpenAPI specification; its integration surface is the device SDK. The company holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II attestations. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead (a16z, Kleiner Perkins, Obvious Ventures).

providers.name: RACE Protocol
providers.description: RACE Protocol is a multi-chain, on-chain infrastructure for developing and deploying secure and fair web3 games. It is delivered primarily through a TypeScript/JavaScript SDK (sdk-core, sdk-solana, sdk-sui, sdk-facade) and a command-line tool (race-cli) for game bundle publishing, account management, and payment claims, rather than as a traditional REST API. Smart contracts run on Solana and Sui.

providers.name: 360 VUZ
providers.description: VUZ (360 VUZ) is an immersive social video platform delivering live and on-demand 360-degree and VR content across sports, concerts, entertainment, celebrities, travel, and master classes. Viewers get exclusive immersive access to top events on mobile, tablet, desktop, and VR headsets including Apple Vision Pro. Founded in the MENA region with headquarters in Riyadh (KAFD) and offices in Dubai, Amman, and Los Angeles, VUZ is backed by 500 Global among other investors. For content partners and creators, VUZ exposes a Creator API (documented via a public Postman collection at creatorapi.360vuz.com) used to publish and manage immersive video. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: OptimizerAI
providers.description: OptimizerAI is an AI-powered sound effects (SFX) foundation model that generates unlimited, high-quality, royalty-free audio from text prompts or reference audio, built for game developers, video producers, filmmakers, and other creators. Its text-to-SFX v2 model produces studio-quality stereo output at 44.1 kHz up to 60 seconds long, with sound variations, style selection, and a "magic prompt" mode that interprets situational descriptions. OptimizerAI, Inc. offers a commercial API on tiered dedicated/shared plans with SLA guarantees, authenticated with a project-specific API key sent over an HTTPS header. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z).

providers.name: Supercell
providers.description: Supercell is the Finnish mobile game developer behind Clash of Clans, Clash Royale, Brawl Stars, Hay Day, Boom Beach and Squad Busters. Supercell operates three official public game APIs — the Clash of Clans API, the Clash Royale API and the Brawl Stars API — that expose read-only game data including clan search, global and local leaderboards, player and clan profiles, leagues, cards, brawlers, rankings and live events. Access is authenticated with a JWT bearer API token created in each game's developer portal and locked to a set of whitelisted IP addresses. Added to the API Evangelist network from a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with verified developer-surface artifacts.

providers.name: Streamloots
providers.description: Streamloots is a monetization platform for live-streaming creators and their communities, originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. It lets streamers turn viewers into paying supporters through interactive collectible Cards that trigger on-stream moments, plus Subscriptions, Auctions, a Marathon goal timer, and Tips. The platform works across Twitch, YouTube, Kick, Facebook, and Trovo, offers creator-favorable revenue splits and bi-monthly payouts, and provides fraud protection, a points store, and browser/OBS alert overlays. Streamloots runs a backend API at api.streamloots.com that powers its apps and Twitch Extension, but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Interplay Learning
providers.description: Interplay Learning is an Austin, Texas edtech company delivering always-on, immersive skilled trades training through online video courses, 3D simulations, and VR for HVAC, plumbing, electrical, facilities maintenance, and solar. Its SkillMill platform has trained more than 500,000 workers to be job-ready, pairing hands-on simulations with custom learning paths, certification prep, and skill assessments. For employers, Interplay exposes an enterprise data-integration API plus SSO and LMS integrations so training data can flow into an organization's own systems; it publishes no public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI. Backed by Sierra Ventures. This profile was enriched from the company's public web surface.

providers.name: Thinglink
providers.description: Thinglink is an educational technology company offering a no-code, AI-powered platform for creating and deploying immersive, interactive learning experiences. Users enrich images, videos, and 360deg / virtual-tour media with clickable "tags" that surface text, audio, links, and embedded content, producing multimodal content for XR, AR, and 360deg training that runs on any device. Thinglink serves K-12 and higher education as well as corporate learning and safety-training teams, and integrates with learning-management systems. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Thinglink publishes a public trust center (ISO 27001, GDPR) but exposes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Gameforge
providers.description: Gameforge AG is a German publisher of free-to-play online and browser games, headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany. Its catalog includes long-running titles such as OGame, Ikariam, Metin2, AION, NosTale, and other strategy and MMO games played across dozens of localized game servers. Gameforge's flagship title OGame exposes a public read-only game-data API that returns highscores, player and alliance rosters, universe/planet layouts, and per-server metadata as XML feeds (with an opt-in JSON representation), plus a separate access-controlled API that approved third-party tool developers can request for combat and report data. Gameforge also runs a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program through Bugcrowd. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: tldraw
providers.description: tldraw is an infinite-canvas SDK for building whiteboard and canvas applications. The primary distribution is the `tldraw` React component package; tldraw also offers a multiplayer sync server. License is the tldraw SDK License (free with watermark for small businesses; paid commercial license to remove watermark).

providers.name: Zed
providers.description: Zed is an open-source, high-performance multiplayer code editor written from scratch in Rust and built around GPU-accelerated rendering through its own GPUI framework. Created by Zed Industries — founded by Nathan Sobo, Antonio Scandurra, and Max Brunsfeld, the team behind Atom, Electron, and Tree-sitter — Zed combines a native desktop editor with real-time collaboration, native Git integration, Language Server Protocol and Debug Adapter Protocol support, and a first-class AI agent surface that includes edit prediction powered by the open-weight Zeta2 model, an inline assistant, parallel agents, and integrations with external coding agents (Claude, Codex, OpenCode) via the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) and Model Context Protocol (MCP). The editor itself is free and triple-licensed (AGPL / Apache-2.0 / GPL-3.0) with paid Pro and Business tiers that bundle hosted AI capabilities, edit prediction quotas, organization controls, and data governance. Zed runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows and exposes a WASM-based extension API (themes, languages, debuggers, snippets, MCP servers, agent servers) with extensions published through the zed-industries/extensions repository.

providers.name: Oculus
providers.description: Oculus is the virtual-reality company founded in 2012 that Kickstarter-launched the Rift headset and was backed by Spark Capital, Matrix Partners and others before Facebook acquired it in 2014 for roughly two billion dollars. The Oculus consumer brand has since been folded into Meta Quest, and the Oculus developer platform now lives as the Meta Horizon developer program at developers.meta.com/horizon. It offers the Oculus/Meta Platform SDK, the Meta Spatial SDK, OpenXR-native, Unity and Unreal engine integrations, and Immersive Web tooling for building mixed- and virtual-reality apps for Horizon OS and the Horizon Store. The oculus.com domain now redirects to Meta Quest, and developer.oculus.com redirects to the Meta Horizon developer portal.

providers.name: RealWear
providers.description: RealWear builds rugged, hands-free head-mounted and assisted-reality wearable computers (the Navigator series and HMT-1) for frontline and industrial workers in energy, manufacturing, field service, and utilities. Its Android-based devices are operated entirely by voice through the on-device WearHF service, which turns any Android app's touch controls into voice commands and can be tuned with WearML voice directives placed in UI metadata — so there is no separate SDK to install. RealWear now also ships Ari, a voice-first AI assistant (Ari OS and the Ari Cloud dashboard) with Microsoft connectors (Teams, Outlook email and calendar, contacts, Copilot), skills, and cross-session memory. Developers extend the platform with native Android, Unity, React Native, Cordova, Xamarin, and HTML apps plus custom Ari skills. This profile was surfaced as a Foundry Group portfolio company and enriched from RealWear's public developer surface.

providers.name: Live Aware Labs
providers.description: Live Aware Labs (LIVE AWARE) is a virtual playtesting and player-insights lab for game studios and researchers. The platform consolidates gameplay footage, player feedback, and community discussion from sources such as Discord, Twitch, YouTube, and internal playtests into a single dashboard, then applies AI to surface trends, player sentiment, and critical feedback in real time. A PC-based SDK captures video, telemetry, and in-game events, with plugins for Unreal Engine and Unity and no-code integrations into Slack, Jira, Monday.com, and OBS. Live Aware Labs is backed by a16z and was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; this profile is enriched from the company's public web surface.

providers.name: Cartwheel
providers.description: Cartwheel is a generative motion platform for games, film & TV, advertising, and robotics. It gives creators a new way to animate 3D characters — turning ordinary video into clean, usable character motion (video-to-motion), and posing and rendering characters as images in any visual style. Cartwheel is delivered as a hosted web studio (studio.getcartwheel.com) with exportable animation formats for downstream 3D, game, film, and social pipelines. The product is in private beta and is backed by Accel, Craft Ventures, and Menlo Ventures. At this time Cartwheel exposes no public developer/REST API; this profile captures its public web, documentation, and security surface.

providers.name: Jagex
providers.description: Jagex is a British video game developer and publisher headquartered in Cambridge, England, best known as the studio behind RuneScape and Old School RuneScape - persistent, community-shaped online worlds that have run for over two decades. Beyond the games, Jagex operates a set of public, read-only RuneScape web-data APIs: the Grand Exchange item price and catalogue endpoints (for both RuneScape and Old School RuneScape), the RuneScape and Old School RuneScape Hiscores, and the RuneMetrics player-profile service. These unauthenticated JSON and CSV endpoints power a large third-party ecosystem of price trackers, fan sites, clan tools, and community applications. Jagex was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners.

providers.name: Maya
providers.description: A collection of APIs for Maya, the popular 3D animation and modeling software developed by Autodesk, providing scripting and plugin development capabilities through Python, C++, MEL, and .NET interfaces.

providers.name: Razer
providers.description: Razer is a global lifestyle brand for gamers that designs gaming hardware (Blade laptops, mice, keyboards, headsets and other peripherals), software (Synapse, Cortex) and services. For developers Razer operates the WYVRN immersive gaming platform, exposing the Razer Chroma RGB SDK and REST API for controlling 16.8-million-color lighting across devices, the Razer Sensa HD Haptics and THX Spatial Audio SDKs, Razer ID for user sign-in, and the Razer Gold / Razer Silver virtual-currency payment and rewards APIs for in-app monetization across 34,000+ integrated games and apps.

providers.name: Tech Soft 3D
providers.description: Tech Soft 3D builds developer SDKs and enterprise applications that power 3D data exchange, visualization, and analysis across engineering, manufacturing, and design. Its HOOPS toolkits (Exchange for CAD data translation and access, Visualize for high-performance 3D graphics, Access, Mesh, Solve, and Envision) are licensed to OEMs and independent developers building CAD, CAM, CAE, and PLM software, and it also distributes Siemens Parasolid and Polygonica. Alongside the native toolkits it publishes the HOOPS Visualize Web Components (open, first-party npm packages), SpinFire enterprise viewing/conversion apps, and OEM technologies such as AutoCAD OEM, Inventor OEM, and RealDWG. Tech Soft 3D is backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Floreo
providers.description: Floreo is a research-based virtual reality (VR) digital therapeutics company that delivers immersive lessons teaching social, behavioral, communication, and life skills to neurodiverse individuals, including autistic children and adults. The platform runs across mobile (iPhone with Google Cardboard) and standalone VR headsets (Meta Quest 2/3/Pro, PICO), with a companion clinician portal for supervised sessions, progress tracking, and telehealth-style delivery. Floreo holds an FDA Breakthrough Device designation and participates in the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP), and works with schools, behavioral-health providers, Medicaid programs, and research partners. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: OPGG
providers.description: OP.GG is the world's leading League of Legends statistics and performance tracking platform. Founded in Seoul, South Korea and launched in 2013, it grew from a LoL stats search engine into a global gaming platform serving tens of millions of monthly active users across games including League of Legends, Valorant, Teamfight Tactics, Overwatch 2, and PUBG. OP.GG surfaces summoner ranks, win rates, champion mastery, builds, tier lists, match history, and live meta trends. Its programmatic surface centers on an official, hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives AI agents access to LoL, TFT, and Valorant game data, plus first-party AI-readable ai.json summoner/match snapshot endpoints advertised in its published llms.txt. OP.GG is backed by 500 Global, SBVA, DS Asset Management, Dunamu & Partners, and others.

providers.name: All3D
providers.description: ALL3D, Inc. is a San Francisco AI-powered visual content platform that replaces traditional product photography for ecommerce brands and agencies. Users upload a product photo and its real-world dimensions, build a scene from inspiration images and props, and generate 4K studio and lifestyle images, influencer/UGC-style video, editable 3D models, 360-degree spins, product configurators, and AR "view in room" experiences accurate to real-world scale. Additional tools cover magic erase, item replacement, scale adjustment, bulk generation across hundreds of SKUs, team review/approval workflows, and direct publishing to Shopify and Amazon. Enterprise plans add API access and managed services. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Codewisp
providers.description: Codewisp is an AI-powered game creation platform that lets anyone build and publish real web games from natural-language prompts, with no coding or game-development tools required. Users describe the game they want and the platform generates the code, structure, and assets automatically, supporting 2D, 3D, and multiplayer browser games with instant, prompt-driven refinement. Founded by game developer Elvin Fu and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch, Codewisp reports 2,000+ weekly active creators and 17,000+ games created, offering a browser-based block editor, a community explore and marketplace surface, and shareable instant-play links. Codewisp is a consumer creation product and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Motif
providers.description: Motif is an AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) software company building an intelligent, browser-based workspace for building design. Founded in 2023 by former Autodesk leaders Amar Hanspal and Brian Mathews, Motif unifies sheet review, live 3D streaming, AI-assisted visual exploration, and real-time collaboration in a single cloud platform that bridges 2D and 3D workflows as a step toward making Building Information Modeling (BIM) a practical reality. The company has raised $46M led by Redpoint Ventures (seed) and Alphabet's CapitalG (Series A), and was named to Forbes' 2025 Next Billion-Dollar Startups list. Motif is a collaboration SaaS product for design and construction teams; it publishes product learning docs and a help center but does not yet expose a public developer API — a plugin/API surface is part of its stated long-term strategy.

providers.name: Kodable
providers.description: Kodable is a San Diego, California based educational technology company that makes self-guided coding, computer science, and digital literacy games for elementary school students in grades K-5. Its product line includes Kodable Basics (an introduction to programming concepts for pre-readers), Kodable Creator (game design and coding with AI-assisted tutoring), Kodable Typing (keyboarding practice), and Bug World (JavaScript and object-oriented programming). Kodable sells to elementary schools and districts as well as directly to parents, pairing the student games with a teacher dashboard, K-5 curriculum, lesson plans, and professional development. The company is a Student Privacy Pledge signatory and a member of the Student Data Privacy Consortium, and publishes a privacy center covering COPPA, its EULA, terms of service, and district Data Privacy Agreement review. Kodable was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Kodable publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts - it is a consumer and school facing application rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Electronic Arts
providers.description: Electronic Arts (EA) is a global leader in digital interactive entertainment, developing and delivering games, content, and online services for internet-connected consoles, mobile devices, and personal computers. EA's portfolio includes franchises such as EA SPORTS FC, Madden NFL, Battlefield, The Sims, Apex Legends, and Need for Speed, supported by online services like EA app, EA Play, and Origin. EA does not currently publish a public developer API portal; integrations and data exchanges are handled through partner programs and the EA Help support and account surfaces.

providers.name: General Intuition
providers.description: General Intuition is a frontier AI lab building large action foundation models that can perceive, predict, and act across space and time in both virtual and physical environments. Spun out of the gaming clip platform Medal, the company trains its spatial-temporal reasoning models on billions of action-labeled gameplay clips - recordings of exactly which buttons a player pressed and when - to teach AI agents how to move through and reason about the world. Its Mira world model powers applications across games, simulation, and robotics. Founded in 2025 and based in New York City, General Intuition has raised $454M total, including a $320M Series A at a $2.3B valuation, and is onboarding first partners to a commercial API ahead of a broader developer release.

providers.name: Simulmedia
providers.description: Simulmedia is a technology-driven television advertising company that helps advertisers, agencies, and growth marketers plan, buy, and measure campaigns across linear TV, connected TV (CTV), and games. Its products include the Performance TV media-buying service, the AI-powered TV+ media-buying platform, and Simulmedia Self-Serve. Through PlayerWON, Simulmedia operates an in-game rewarded-video engagement and monetization platform for free-to-play console and PC games, exposed to game developers through the PlayerWON API and a first-party Unity/Unreal SDK. Simulmedia is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the company's public developer surface and the open-source PlayerWON SDK.

providers.name: Zibra AI
providers.description: Zibra AI is a Ukrainian deep-tech company building AI-powered real-time volumetric rendering and compression technology for VFX, gaming, virtual production, film, and TV. Its flagship product, ZibraVDB, compresses OpenVDB volumetric datasets to roughly five percent of their original size while preserving visual quality, enabling real-time playback of smoke, fire, fog, and other volumetric effects. Zibra ships a native C++ ZibraVDB SDK (DirectX 12, Vulkan, and Metal on Windows, Linux, and macOS) alongside plugins for Unreal Engine, Houdini, and Unity, with Blender support in progress. It exposes no public REST/HTTP API; integration is through the SDK and digital-content-creation plugins. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rockstar Games
providers.description: Rockstar Games is an American video game publisher headquartered in New York City and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Take-Two Interactive Software (NASDAQ: TTWO). Best known for the Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption franchises, Rockstar operates online services for GTA Online and Red Dead Online, the Rockstar Games Launcher PC client, and the legacy Rockstar Games Social Club identity / authentication platform. Rockstar does not publish a public developer portal; its HTTP API surface is internal and consumed only by first-party clients (game executables, the Rockstar Games Launcher, and Rockstar's mobile companion apps). The most visible public-facing API is its OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 identity provider at signin.rockstargames.com, which exposes standard /connect/authorize, /connect/Token, /connect/introspect, and /.well-known/jwks endpoints. Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to launch on November 19, 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S and will include a "significant online mode" succeeding GTA Online.

providers.name: NAVER Z
providers.description: NAVER Z Corporation is the South Korean metaverse subsidiary of NAVER, headquartered in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, with additional offices in Los Angeles and Tokyo. The company builds immersive digital experiences spanning ZEPETO, its avatar-based metaverse and social app launched in 2018; ZEP, a spatial collaboration and virtual-space platform launched in 2022; and Sticker.ly, a sticker creation and sharing app launched in 2019. NAVER Z's public developer surface is ZEP Script: a first-party JavaScript SDK, CLI, and build toolchain (published on npm under the official @zep.us scope) that creators use to build in-space apps and mini-games, documented in the ZEP Guidebook at docs.zep.us with a dedicated ZEP Script API reference. NAVER Z publishes no REST/OpenAPI web API or OAuth program; ZEPETO Studio remains a Unity-based content-creation tool rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Take-Two Interactive Software
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Take-Two Interactive Software API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Play Versus
providers.description: Play Versus (PlayVS) is North America's leading scholastic and collegiate esports platform, operating competitive gaming leagues for middle schools, high schools, and colleges alongside an esports curriculum and college recruitment services. The platform partners with major publishers including Riot Games, EA, Blizzard, and Psyonix, and runs its competitions and rosters through the app.playvs.com web application. PlayVS is a consumer/education product and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface; this profile captures its published identity, support, and policy properties. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sira Medical
providers.description: Sira Medical develops augmented reality software that transforms 3D radiological imaging into patient-specific holographic models projected onto real-world backgrounds. Delivered through head-mounted AR devices (such as Microsoft HoloLens) and mobile platforms, the technology helps surgeons perform preoperative planning with greater confidence, clinicians educate patients with understandable visualizations, medical schools train students on patient-specific anatomy, and medical-device makers design and validate implants. The company is backed by 500 Global, Eileses Capital, UCSF Innovation Ventures, and Microsoft for Startups. Sira Medical operates as a clinical AR software vendor and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: App Onboard
providers.description: AppOnBoard, Inc. is a Los Angeles-based technology company founded in 2016 that builds AI-driven creative and advertising tools for app and game marketers. Its best-known product is Buildbox, a no-code platform for making games and apps without programming, and its current flagship is Quvy, an AI ad-creation and testing platform that generates static, video, and concept ad variations and predicts their performance against synthetic audiences before any real ad spend. Quvy targets marketers, indie and studio game developers, SaaS companies, and brands that want to replace slow, expensive A/B testing and agencies with fast simulation-based creative optimization. AppOnBoard is backed by 500 Global; its original apponboard.com domain now redirects to the Quvy product at quvy.com. This profile carries the company identity and website properties; AppOnBoard publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: DIY
providers.description: DIY.org is a safe, ad-free creative platform where kids turn ideas into real games, apps, and websites — guided by AI tools like Vibe Coding and KidsGPT and reviewed by human moderators. Serving over 500,000 young creators, it pairs game-building templates, AI image and art tools, badge-based learning, and 75+ standards-aligned courses with parent and classroom dashboards, SSO, and safety controls. Originally a maker community for kids, DIY is backed by Kleiner Perkins and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: Eksab
providers.description: Eksab is a Cairo-based daily fantasy sports and football-prediction platform for the MENA region. Founded in 2017 by Aly Mahmoud, it lets fans predict the scores and outcomes of live football matches, earn points based on the accuracy of their picks, and win prizes through free and paid competitions. The platform has grown to over 700,000 registered users making more than a million picks each month, and in 2022 became the exclusive fantasy sports partner of the Egyptian Premier League. Eksab is backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), 4DX Ventures, and others across roughly $3.7M in seed funding. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Eksab is a consumer mobile/web product and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Track Titan
providers.description: Track Titan is a sim racing analytics and coaching platform that records in-game telemetry from simulators including iRacing, Assetto Corsa and ACC, the F1 series, Automobilista 2, Forza Motorsport, and Le Mans Ultimate, turning laps into time-loss analysis, AI coaching feedback, auto-installed esports car setups, and structured Academy learning content for a community of over 295,000 sim racers on PC and console. Founded by former professional sim racer and Porsche coach Max Teichert and backed by investors including Partech, Track Titan is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of July 2026 (api.tracktitan.io serves only an internal backend service).

providers.name: Matcherino
providers.description: Matcherino is an esports crowdfunding and tournament-management platform that provides monetization infrastructure for competitive gaming events of every scale, from college clubs to stadium finals. Its stack covers prize-pool crowdfunding, brackets, player signups, ticketing and entry fees, streaming overlays, sponsor activation, and a publisher dashboard for distributing cash and in-game prizes. Matcherino handles global payouts to organizers and winners across 120+ countries with tax-form collection, and surfaces real-time analytics for organizers, sponsors, and publishers. The company reports having paid out more than $5.2M across 14,000+ tournaments. Matcherino is a Techstars-backed company; it does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Trass Games
providers.description: Trass Games is an a16z-backed independent VR game studio best known for Yeeps - Hide and Seek, a free-to-play social hide-and-seek and building game on Meta Quest, and Gods of Gravity, an arcade space RTS. The studio ships a Yeeps companion app for iOS and Android, sells plush, maker-kit, and apparel merchandise through Shopify storefronts at yeeps.com and godsofgravityvr.com, and runs a community licensing program for creators. Trass Games publishes no first-party developer API, but its storefronts expose agent-ready commerce surfaces including llms.txt, agents.md, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, and a live storefront MCP endpoint.

providers.name: Immersed
providers.description: Immersed is a spatial-computing company that turns AR/VR headsets into portable multi-monitor workspaces for remote work, coding, and collaboration. Its free desktop agent streams up to five virtual screens into headsets such as Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro, GalaxyXR, and Pico, adding solo focus environments plus multi-user telepresence with screen sharing and whiteboarding. Immersed is also building Visor, its own lightweight 4K-per-eye standalone headset. The company is Techstars-backed. Immersed publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, product, security, and llms.txt surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Machinations
providers.description: Machinations is a visual platform for designing, simulating, and balancing game economies, tokenomics, and other complex systems. Studios and designers model resource flows as interactive node-and-connection diagrams, run Monte-Carlo simulations to predict outcomes, and balance economies before a single line of production code is written. The product spans Design, Predict, and Balance modules plus an AI Builder that generates runnable diagrams from natural-language descriptions and a spreadsheet integration. It is used by studios such as Amazon Games, Hasbro, and Zynga and taught at MIT, NYU, and Berkeley. Machinations is a Seedcamp portfolio company; at the time of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Parallel Universe
providers.description: Parallel Universe Inc. (Parallel Studios) is the Toronto-based game studio behind Parallel, a free-to-play sci-fi trading card game, and the broader Parallel Universe franchise that includes Colony, an AI agent simulation game, and Sanctuary, a third-person extraction shooter. The studio anchors the Echelon Prime web3 gaming ecosystem, where players truly own their cards and in-game items as blockchain assets and the PRIME token powers governance and rewards. Backed by a16z (Andreessen Horowitz) and Paradigm, Parallel is a consumer game franchise distributed via the web, Epic Games, Steam, the Apple App Store, and Google Play. It publishes no public developer / REST API surface today; this profile captures the studio's public web, community, and legal properties as harvested by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Over
providers.description: Overworld is an open-science AI research lab building interactive world models - AI-generated video environments that respond in real time to text prompts and controller input at game-level framerates. Its open-source World Engine is a Python inference library that loads Waypoint world models and LoRA adapters from HuggingFace to generate playable, promptable worlds locally or in the browser. Founded by Louis Castricato (CEO) and Shahbuland Matiana (Head of Mathematical Research), both formerly of CarperAI and Stability AI, the team operates openly and publishes its infrastructure as public open-source repositories. Overworld does not currently expose a hosted REST API; its primary developer artifact is the first-party world_engine Python SDK.

providers.name: Primodium Inc.
providers.description: Primodium Inc. (primodiumxyz) is a developer-focused studio building fully on-chain applications and games on Ethereum and Solana. It ships two on-chain games — Primodium, a space-based factory-building game, and Primodium: Empires, a turn-based prediction-market game — both built with MUD and Phaser, alongside a suite of open-source developer libraries and infrastructure: Reactive Tables (a strictly-typed reactive table library for MUD apps), a Solana DEX Indexer Stack exposing a GraphQL API over Hasura/Timescale, a tRPC transaction-sponsoring DEX server, an off-chain MUD indexer, and gasless-transaction relayers. All tooling is published open-source under the MIT license via the primodiumxyz GitHub organization and the @primodiumxyz npm scope.

providers.name: Manticore Games
providers.description: Manticore Games is a San Mateo-based game developer and publisher, and the studio behind Core — a free, Unreal Engine-powered game-creation platform and metaverse where a global community of creators builds, publishes, and plays multiplayer games and experiences. Core exposes a rich Lua scripting API (namespaces, types, and events for Players, Weapons, Abilities, Storage, Leaderboards, Chat, UI, and World) that lets creators program game logic directly in the editor. Manticore is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund.

providers.name: Regression Games
providers.description: Regression Games builds AI agents and bots for video games. Its platform lets studios create bots for QA testing, multiplayer simulation, game balancing, and NPC behavior with minimal code. The Unity SDK (gg.regression.unity.bots / RGUnityBots) adds AI-driven automated playtesting, UI and screenshot regression testing, replay and validation, and CI/CD integration for Unity projects, while the earlier rg-bot JavaScript/TypeScript/Python libraries let developers program bots for Minecraft and Capture-the-Flag tournaments. Distribution is via open-source SDKs and templates on GitHub rather than a hosted public REST API. Backed by a16z and NEA ($4.2M seed, 2022).

providers.name: Pinscreen
providers.description: Pinscreen is an American AI and VFX production company founded in 2015 by Hao Li (MIT TR35 winner and professor of computer vision at MBZUAI), headquartered in Los Angeles with a branch in Abu Dhabi (UAE). It builds advanced generative AI for film production and interactive experiences, including AI lip sync, face reenactment, face swaps, de-aging, voice cloning, and photoreal 3D avatar digitization, and is known for developing the world's first real-time deepfake technology. Its Avatar Neo product generates a photoreal, riggable 3D avatar from a single photo (exportable as GLB/FBX with animation rigs) and is offered to developers as the Avatar Neo SDK: Unreal and Unity engine plugins backed by an avatar-generation API that can be deployed anywhere. Customers include Netflix, Amazon Studios, Warner Bros, Miramax, Apple, Google, Adobe, and DARPA. Backed by Lux Capital and Middle East investors.

providers.name: Sanlo
providers.description: Sanlo is a multi-platform payments and monetization platform built specifically for game developers and studios.
