Its products let studios run live ops and accept payments outside the walled gardens of the major app stores to reduce platform commission fees: Webshop Builder (a full-stack direct-to-consumer web shop), Web Checkout (accept payments on any website, web shop, or web game), and Unity Checkout (native iOS/Android in-game checkout for Unity titles via a first-party SDK and API, with one-click checkout, fully customizable UI, and creator-code support). Card and payment collection is powered by Adyen underneath. Sanlo also offers game funding to help studios finance user acquisition and growth. The company is backed by Index Ventures and other gaming-focused investors.

providers.name: Tap
providers.description: TAP (Training All People, Inc.) is a next-generation technician training platform for advanced and precision manufacturers. TAP combines online courses (pneumatics, electrical fundamentals, robotics, safety, and semiconductor basics) with immersive VR simulations that replicate real factory equipment and procedures, plus in-simulation quizzes, VR scenario assessments, and workforce skills-profiling dashboards. The platform lets manufacturers evaluate, standardize, and upskill their technician workforce at scale while minimizing disruption to production. Customers include Northrop Grumman, ACC, SUNY, and Dallas College. Backed by 8vc and surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company; TAP currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: FanDuel
providers.description: FanDuel is a major US sports betting and daily fantasy sports operator (FanDuel Sportsbook, FanDuel Casino, FanDuel Fantasy, FanDuel TV). FanDuel does not publish a public developer REST API for its sportsbook, casino, or fantasy products. Internal/private APIs power the apps and a Sportradar/SBTech-derived trading stack but are not available to third-party developers.

providers.name: PrizePicks
providers.description: PrizePicks is a US daily-fantasy/pick-em sports operator focused on player-prop projections (more/less). PrizePicks does not publish a public developer REST API. Internal/private endpoints power the web and mobile apps but are not documented or licensed for third-party use.

providers.name: Backbone
providers.description: Backbone is a mobile gaming company that makes the Backbone One controller — a snap-on gamepad for iPhone and Android — and the Backbone app, a mobile gaming platform that unifies a player's game library across cloud gaming, console Remote Play, and streaming services with game discovery, capture, and social features. The company sells hardware and accessories through a Shopify-hosted storefront (backbone.com) that exposes an agent-commerce surface via the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint and Shopify Customer Account OIDC. Backbone is a portfolio company of Index Ventures. This profile was enriched from Backbone's public web surface; the company publishes no first-party developer API.

providers.name: Goals
providers.description: Goals (playgoals.com, formerly goals.co) is a free-to-play competitive football (soccer) video game studio backed by Northzone. It positions itself as a gameplay-first football game — "No scripts, no excuses, just football" — with fast, skill-based competitive matches, unique player squads, card-pack collection, ranked leaderboards, and multiple game modes across Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, and the Epic Games Store. A companion app lets players manage squads and open packs. This profile was surfaced as a Northzone portfolio company (consumer sector) and added to the API Evangelist network; the studio publishes a consumer game and a community surface (Discord, guides, leaderboards) but no public developer API.

providers.name: Squint
providers.description: Squint is a Manufacturing Intelligence platform that uses AI and augmented reality to help industrial and frontline operations teams lower downtime and improve quality at scale. Its mobile app captures and digitizes tribal knowledge from video and real work, orchestrates workflows and work assignments across employees and locations, provides AI-powered troubleshooting and expert guidance, and delivers analytics on performance across teams and sites. Founded by Devin Bhushan, Squint began in manufacturing and serves automotive, food and beverage, oil and gas, heavy industrials, equipment, consumer packaged goods, and energy customers, expanding into healthcare and hospitality. Backed by Menlo Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Squint exposes no public developer API; its documentation and application are gated behind a Squint workspace login.

providers.name: Dreamforge
providers.description: DreamForge.ai is an AI-powered game creation platform for building, iterating on, and publishing 2D and stylized 3D games directly in the browser. Creators use AI to generate gameplay systems, game-ready art and textures, animation, and playable web builds, then share public play pages under dreamforge.ai/play. The platform pairs a creator-facing web studio (including an Asset Studio) with a consumer application distributed on Steam, iOS, and Android. Founded in 2025 and based in Miami, Florida, DreamForge is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). DreamForge supports stylized 3D world generation, textures, voxels, and billboarding workflows; native 3D model generation is not currently provided. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published at this time.

providers.name: NeonRain, Inc.
providers.description: NeonRain, Inc. is a 500 Global portfolio company whose public product surface resolves to Playabl (playabl.ai), an AI-powered, no-code platform that lets anyone create web games and interactive experiences by chatting with AI. Users describe a game idea in plain English and Playabl's generative AI produces a playable prototype instantly, which can be refined conversationally and published to the web. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in the United States, the product targets educators, indie developers, marketers, and hobbyists. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer web application with no developer-facing API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: The Meta
providers.description: The Meta is the gaming-performance company behind KovaaK's Aim Trainer (formerly "Kovaak 2.0: The Meta"), a PC esports training platform distributed on Steam that pairs guided, skill-specific training modules with Kovaak's Sandbox aim trainer and its library of 2,600+ user-generated scenarios. The platform lets FPS players measure, diagnose, and improve their mechanical aim and in-game habits, feeding back insights on weaknesses so players can target their practice. Founded by Duncan Haberly, Jay Brown, and Chris Olson and backed by Canaan (Beta Fund), Village Global, Courtside VC, betaworks, GFR, and Akatsuki Entertainment Technology (AET Fund). The Meta operates a consumer game product, a community wiki, and a Discord community; it does not currently publish a public first-party developer API.

providers.name: Gankster
providers.description: Gankster is a consumer competitive-gaming social platform — a web and mobile "looking for group" (LFG) network that helps players team up, practice, and compete across titles including Valorant, League of Legends, Dota 2, Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League, Fortnite, and World of Warcraft. It matches players by rank, playstyle, and reputation to find duos, five-stacks, and fill players, and lets teams organize scrims, tournaments, and recruitment. Gankster operates entirely outside the game client (no overlays or client modifications) and ships the Gankster Duos mobile app on iOS and Android. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and raised $4.25M for its all-in-one competitive gaming platform. Gankster does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Genopets
providers.description: Genopets is a free-to-play, move-to-earn NFT game built on the Solana blockchain that gamifies an active lifestyle. Players nurture a digital pet — a Genopet — that evolves from real-world physical activity tracked via step counting, then battle, craft, stake, and trade in-game NFTs and Habitats. The economy pairs the GENE governance token with the in-game KI utility token earned by moving. Genopets is developed by a studio backed by Pantera Capital and operates a consumer mobile/web game rather than a public developer API; no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: FanCraze
providers.description: FanCraze is an International Cricket Council (ICC) officially licensed platform for cricket collectibles, trading, and fantasy gaming, serving more than 500,000 cricket fans worldwide. Its flagship products are Grails, a digital collectibles experience where fans pull officially licensed ICC player cards (Common through Legendary), trade them with other fans, and complete themed sets; and Matchday, a free-to-play fantasy cricket game where fans build squads from their collectibles and compete on live challenges tied to real ICC tournaments including Men's and Women's Cricket World Cups, T20 World Cups, and U-19 World Cups. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and is backed by investors including Tiger Global, Sequoia, Coatue, Dapper Labs, and Coinbase Ventures. FanCraze operates as a consumer (B2C) mobile and web app and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Dapperlabs
providers.description: Dapper Labs is a Vancouver-based blockchain company (originally spun out of Axiom Zen) that builds consumer crypto and NFT experiences and the developer platform behind them. It created the Flow blockchain, CryptoKitties, and the Dapper Wallet, and operates licensed digital-collectible marketplaces including NBA Top Shot, NFL All Day, LaLiga Golazos, UFC Strike, and Disney Pinnacle. Its developer surface ("Dapper Core") exposes Cadence smart contracts, the Dapper Wallet / Dapper Connect authentication flow, and Flow blockchain SDKs so third parties can build on top of Dapper's collectibles and on-chain assets rather than through a traditional REST/OpenAPI API.

providers.name: Dare Drop
providers.description: Dare Drop is a gaming influencer marketing platform that connects game publishers and brands with content creators across Twitch, YouTube, and TikTok. The platform runs reward-driven "Dares" — challenges that incentivize streamers and creators to produce longer, more engaging content around a title, while automating creator targeting, campaign management, and reporting. Dare Drop offers influencer campaigns, ongoing influencer programs, and organic outreach, and has facilitated over 18,000 publisher Dares and distributed more than 30,000 rewards to creator communities. Its customers include game studios and publishers such as EA, Respawn, Raw Fury, Tencent, Obsidian, and Gearbox. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface has been found to date.

providers.name: Fab.com
providers.description: Fab.com is a digital content marketplace operated by Epic Games, where creators buy and sell 3D models, materials, environments, VFX, audio, and game-ready assets. Launched in October 2024, Fab consolidated four of Epic's prior storefronts — the Unreal Engine Marketplace, the Sketchfab Store, Quixel, and the ArtStation Marketplace — into a single catalog with unified licensing, and integrates into Unreal Engine, UEFN, and the Epic Games Launcher. The fabcom entry was originally added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead for the earlier, unrelated Fab.com flash-sale design-commerce company (2011–2015), which wound down before the domain passed to Epic Games; see x-identity-note. Fab publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification as of this pass — the surface captured here is its documentation, support, and security-disclosure posture.

providers.name: Loft Dynamics
providers.description: Loft Dynamics is a Swiss aviation technology company (founded 2016, headquartered in Dübendorf, Switzerland with a North American office in Santa Monica) that builds virtual reality flight simulation training devices (FSTDs) for helicopters, fixed-wing aircraft, and eVTOLs. Its simulators combine full-scale replica cockpits, dynamic motion platforms, 360-degree VR visuals, and advanced pose tracking, and were the first VR aircraft simulators to earn EASA and FAA qualification. Products include VR simulators for the Airbus H145, Airbus H125, and Robinson R22 helicopters, with Boeing 737 and eVTOL platforms in development. Customers include Alaska Airlines, the FAA, Airbus Helicopters, the LAPD, and Marshall University. The company operates the LoftHUB customer platform but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Lumosity
providers.description: Lumosity is a consumer brain-training platform built by Lumos Labs that offers cognitive games and personalized daily workouts targeting memory, attention, problem solving, flexibility, and processing speed. The service adapts difficulty to individual performance, tracks progress over time, and is delivered through the web and iOS/Android mobile apps. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, the company was surfaced through VC-portfolio discovery; probing its public surface found no developer portal, public API, or documented programmatic integration — it is a direct-to-consumer product with no API surface at this time.

providers.name: Playbite
providers.description: Playbite is a free mobile arcade app - "an arcade in your pocket" - built by Digital Media Technology SL and backed by 500 Global. The app offers an ever-expanding library of simple, casual games spanning multiplayer, rhythm, puzzle, matching, relaxing, and racing categories, with over 500,000 players who play games and earn rewards. The service is free to users and monetized through non-intrusive advertising. Playbite is a consumer-facing mobile gaming product distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures its company identity, public web properties, and domain security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Players Lounge
providers.description: Players' Lounge is a skill-based competitive gaming platform where users win money by completing personalized head-to-head gaming challenges (money matches) or by staking and watching other players compete. The platform supports popular console and PC titles including Madden, NBA 2K, Call of Duty Warzone, Marvel Rivals, and others, and states it has paid out over $200M to players to date. Players' Lounge is a consumer product surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation at this time. This profile captures the company's public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Start Playing
providers.description: StartPlaying (startplaying.games) is the largest online marketplace connecting tabletop roleplaying game (TTRPG) players with professional Game Masters for systems including Dungeons & Dragons, Pathfinder, Starfinder, Warhammer, and many more. Players discover, book, and join online sessions filtered by system, platform, genre, playstyle, and GM reviews, while Game Masters build careers by hosting paid games across virtual tabletops. The platform also offers gift cards, learn-to-play one-shots for beginners, kids' games, and corporate team-building events. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a consumer web product with no public developer API.

providers.name: Wave
providers.description: Wave is a virtual entertainment company that produces interactive, avatar-driven virtual concerts and immersive live music experiences known as "Waves." The platform streams stylized, real-time performances from major recording artists — including The Weeknd, Justin Bieber, John Legend, J Balvin, and Alison Wonderland — as animated avatars across VR headsets, desktop, mobile, and social video platforms, letting fans attend and interact with shows from anywhere. Wave is a consumer-facing entertainment and media product (accessed at wavexr.com) rather than a developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation. It was surfaced as a venture-portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, where this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Atari
providers.description: Atari is one of the founding brands of the interactive entertainment industry, originally established in 1972, and today operates as a global video game and consumer-hardware company. It publishes classic and modern titles, manufactures the Atari VCS console and retro hardware (Atari 2600+, Atari 400 Mini), licenses its catalog and brand, and sells games, collectibles, and merchandise through its official online store at atari.com. Atari does not publish a general-purpose public REST API; its developer surface is limited to Atari VCS content-submission guidance (developers email vcs@atari.com and use the VCS submission portal) and legacy HTML5 Atari Arcade SDK libraries on GitHub. This profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company — a nod to Mayfield's foundational 1970s venture investment in Atari — and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Kixeye
providers.description: KIXEYE Inc. is a video game developer and publisher founded in 2009 and headquartered in Victoria, British Columbia, with staff across Canada and the United States. KIXEYE creates, develops, and publishes massively multiplayer online real-time strategy (MMORTS) games for browsers, tablets, and smartphones, including Battle Pirates, War Commander, War Commander: Rogue Assault, and Rise of Firstborn. An early innovator in the free-to-play genre, KIXEYE operates long-lived live-service game worlds with monthly events, alliances, and competitive leaderboards for millions of players worldwide. KIXEYE is part of the Stillfront Group. KIXEYE publishes no public developer program or partner API; its api.kixeye.com host is a private game-services backend that exposes an OpenID Connect discovery document and JWKS for token verification. The company does maintain a public GitHub organization of open-source infrastructure libraries (chassis, kixmpp, janus, scout) used to build its own cloud services.

providers.name: IrisVR
providers.description: IrisVR is a virtual-reality software company for the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry, best known for its two products: Prospect, a desktop application that converts Revit, SketchUp, Rhino, Navisworks and other 3D/BIM models into immersive VR walkthroughs in one click, and Scope, a mobile app for viewing and sharing 360-degree panoramas on standalone and phone-based VR headsets. Founded in New York, IrisVR was acquired by The Wild in 2021, and The Wild (together with IrisVR) was subsequently acquired by Autodesk in 2022. The products and support site remain available. IrisVR does not publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity, packages, and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Zwift
providers.description: Zwift is a Long Beach, California online fitness company that operates a multiplayer indoor cycling and running platform combining stationary smart trainers and bikes with a 3D virtual-world game client. Riders and runners use a smart trainer, smart bike (such as the in-house Zwift Ride), treadmill, or pod to drive an avatar through fictional worlds (Watopia, Makuri Islands) and licensed real-world routes, joining structured workouts, group rides, races, training plans, and 24/7 events alongside a global community of more than a million members. The platform pairs with smart trainers and heart-rate monitors over Bluetooth and ANT+, and the Zwift Companion mobile app provides in-game messaging, ride control, and route discovery. Zwift does not operate a general public developer portal, OpenAPI reference, or open-source SDK. Its developer surface is limited to a private, application-only Structured Training API for approved training partners (TrainingPeaks, TrainerRoad, Wahoo SYSTM, JOIN Cycling and similar coaching platforms) that lets external workout builders push custom workouts into a rider's Zwift account, plus one-way activity-export connections to Strava, TrainingPeaks, Garmin Connect, MapMyRide, MapMyRun, Adidas Running, Technogym, Fitbit, Wahoo, Apple Health, and Withings. There is no public REST surface, OAuth client registration, or partner self-service available to general developers — third-party tools (community libraries, ZwiftPower, Sauce for Zwift) interact with Zwift via reverse-engineered private endpoints, not a sanctioned API. Zwift is a paid consumer subscription business; revenue comes from monthly memberships and hardware sales (Zwift Ride, Zwift Cog, Zwift Click, Zwift Play).

providers.name: AppliedVR
providers.description: AppliedVR is a virtual reality therapeutics company that combines immersive technology with proven cognitive behavioral and behavioral-science techniques to treat medical conditions, with a focus on chronic pain. Its lead product, RelieVRx, is the first FDA-authorized prescription VR device for chronic lower back pain, delivering automated, self-administered cognitive behavioral therapy in the patient's home. AppliedVR also offers the SustainVR and ITx immersive therapeutics platform and the AVR Pathway patient-support system, and validates its products through clinical academic research. The company operates as a regulated digital-therapeutics / medical-device business rather than a developer-facing API platform, so it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Draxon
providers.description: Draxon is a Berlin-based company (founded 2025, backed by HV Capital and Point Nine) that provides IATA-certified virtual reality training for airport ground handling operations. The platform ships pre-configured Meta Quest VR headsets and an immersive training library covering ramp equipment such as belt loaders, tractors, pushback tugs, GPUs and towable stairs, plus safety procedures and hand signals for frontline ramp personnel. Its Trainer Hub delivers automated, IATA-compliant certification tracking with self-paced or instructor-led modules. Draxon operates as a B2B SaaS training provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: EyeLights
providers.description: EyeLights is a French deep-tech company building augmented reality head-up display (HUD) technology for riders and pilots. Its products project GPS navigation, speed, intercom, radar and call information into the rider's line of sight: EyeRide, a universal HUD accessory compatible with any motorcycle helmet; the GT-AIR 3 Smart, an integrated head-up display visor built into a SHOEI helmet; the APEX HUD glasses for general aviation; and Pulse Ultra, a universal Bluetooth intercom. The company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at eye-lights.com and runs customer support on Odoo. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; EyeLights publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so this record captures its consumer web, identity, and security posture rather than an API contract.

providers.name: Z1
providers.description: Z1 is the API Evangelist network profile for the consumer social gaming app operated by Bunch Live, Inc., known publicly as Bunch and now rebranded as Mini Party (mini.party). The product lets friends hang out, play party games, and video chat together in real time on mobile, and connects with external services such as Discord. Bunch raised early venture funding (including a $3.8M round) and is tracked here as a 500 Global portfolio company. Bunch formerly operated a Bunch Developer Platform (the "Party Kit" voice/video SDK for iOS, Android, and Unity plus a Party Reservation API), but that developer program has been discontinued and the company currently publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal — this profile captures its identity, legal surface, and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Hidden Door
providers.description: Hidden Door is an interactive storytelling platform where roleplay meets fan fiction, letting players step into imaginative worlds and shape branching narratives through their choices. Players pick a pre-built world, add modifiers, create a character, and experience a unique story with a full cast of characters, where every playthrough differs. Creators can build playable worlds in as little as thirty minutes, then share, publish, and get paid when others play. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Homebrew and Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. Hidden Door ships a consumer web experience and publishes no developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. Sector: AI / entertainment.

providers.name: Hyperpad
providers.description: Hyperpad (hyperPad) is a no-code, visual game development platform for iPad, often described as "HyperCard for iPad." Founded in 2013 and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2014), the London, Ontario company lets non-programmers build media-rich 2D games and interactive apps using a drag-and-drop, node-based behavior system with a built-in physics engine, particle effects, animation and audio tools, and a bundled asset library, then publish them to the Apple App Store as native apps while keeping 100% of royalties. Products include the paid hyperPad app, a free hyperPad Starter edition, and hyperPad Hub, a community arcade for playing games made with the platform. hyperPad is a consumer-facing creation tool and does not currently publish a public web API or developer platform.

providers.name: Rosebud AI
providers.description: Rosebud AI is an AI-powered game creation platform that lets anyone build and deploy playable 3D games and interactive worlds from natural-language prompts, a workflow the company calls "Vibe Coding" — you describe scenes, rules, and behaviors and an AI assistant named "Rosie" writes and applies the underlying JavaScript. The platform runs on a custom engine designed for AI-era game development, featuring deterministic WASM-based physics, native real-time multiplayer, instant link-based sharing, and a built-in "Juice API" for camera effects, particle systems, and spatial audio. Founded in 2019 in San Francisco by CEO Lisha Li (Ph.D. in machine learning, UC Berkeley), Rosebud AI is backed by a16z. As of this enrichment pass the company ships a hosted consumer product and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK packages, MCP server, or developer portal.

providers.name: StatusPRO
providers.description: StatusPRO is a sports technology and gaming company founded by former professional athletes, building extended reality (XR) products that pair competitive training tools for elite athletes with immersive gaming experiences for consumers. Its flagship product, NFL PRO ERA, is an officially NFL- and NFLPA-licensed virtual reality football game for Meta Quest headsets, and its StatusPRO Visualizer powers immersive broadcast perspectives used by ESPN on NFL Live. The company operates a live-services consumer game rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record; it carries no API surface at this time.

providers.name: Kidas
providers.description: Kidas is a Techstars-backed trust-and-safety company that builds white-label scam detection and online-protection solutions for enterprises and consumers. Its ProtectMe platform monitors PC gaming and Discord voice and text channels for cyberbullying, predators, phishing, and scams, and its broader suite adds SMS scam detection, email protection, a scam-screening chatbot, and deepfake/impersonation defense that integrate into existing customer channels. Kidas markets custom builds and lists Aura, Comcast, Overwolf, Razer, Walmart, Intel, and Best Buy among its customers. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Prisms VR
providers.description: Prisms VR (Prisms) is an educational technology company building what it calls the world's first spatial learning platform, where students learn core math, science, and other subjects by abstracting up from immersive, first-person physical experiences delivered in virtual reality. Founded by MIT engineer-turned-educator Anurupa Ganguly, the teacher-facing platform uses kinesthetic, embodied learning to help students grasp abstract concepts and aims to develop curious, resilient thinkers. Prisms is an a16z portfolio company; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead and profiled through the enrichment pipeline. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Statespace
providers.description: Statespace is the company behind Aimlabs (aimlabs.com, formerly statespace.gg), the leading AI-powered aim-training platform for FPS gamers. Aimlabs delivers personalized training tasks, real-time performance analytics, and game-specific tools, serving over 40 million players and operating as an official partner of Valorant and Rainbow Six Siege. Statespace is venture-backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Lux Capital. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer web/desktop product but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: ironSource
providers.description: ironSource is a Tel Aviv-based mobile game growth platform, acquired by Unity Technologies in a $4.4B all-stock deal that closed in November 2022 and is now operated as part of Unity's Grow Solutions group. The company builds an end-to-end suite for mobile game developers spanning ad monetization, user acquisition, and ad operations. Its flagship product LevelPlay is a unified in-app bidding and ad mediation platform that brokers Rewarded Video, Interstitial, and Banner ad demand across the ironSource Ads network, AdMob, AppLovin, Meta Audience Network, Pangle, Mintegral, Unity Ads, Vungle, and dozens of other ad sources. ironSource Ads is its self-serve ad network and user-acquisition platform offering CPI, CPE, ROAS-optimized, and SKAdNetwork-aware campaign management. Adjacent products include Aura (an on-device content marketplace for carriers and OEMs that originated from the 2021 Bigabid/Soomla portfolio and earlier hardware OEM deals), Tapjoy Offerwall (acquired 2022) for rewarded engagement, and Ad Quality for ad-content monitoring. Developer access is via a REST surface hosted at platform.ironsrc.com — including the Monetization Reporting API (v5/v4), ironSource Ads Reporting API, Application API (v6), Campaign API suite (Campaigns, Audiences, Country Groups, Bidding, Assets, Creatives), SKAN Reporting API, and Cost API — authenticated with Bearer tokens issued from the platform dashboard. Real client integration is delivered via native SDKs (iOS, Android, Unity, Flutter, React Native, Adobe AIR, Xamarin) plus the LevelPlay mediation adapter ecosystem published on github.com/ironsource-mobile. As of 2026 the developers.is.com knowledge center 301-redirects to docs.unity.com, consolidating ironSource documentation inside Unity Grow alongside Unity Ads. No public OpenAPI, Postman collection, or JSON Schema bundle is published by ironSource for the REST surface; documentation is human-readable HTML on docs.unity.com/en-us/grow.

providers.name: Medivis
providers.description: Medivis is a medical technology company building AI-powered augmented reality solutions for surgery and medical education. Its flagship product, SurgicalAR, is an FDA 510(k)-cleared platform that runs on Microsoft HoloLens 2 and transforms 2D medical imaging (CT and MRI) into interactive 3D holographic visualizations for surgical planning and navigation, including FDA-cleared systems for spine and cranial procedures. Medivis also offers AnatomyX, an AR platform for anatomy and medical education. The company reports deployment across 40+ institutions and use in 2,000+ surgeries. Medivis is a Microsoft technology partner and a portfolio company of Initialized Capital. Medivis publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; its software surface is delivered as HoloLens and iOS applications for clinical and educational users.

providers.name: Mira
providers.description: Mira is a San Francisco-based consumer hardware startup building AI-powered smart glasses positioned as an always-on "second brain." Founded in 2024 by Harvard builders AnhPhu Nguyen and Caine Ardayfio (rebranded from Halo), the camera-free glasses pair a dual-waveguide display, microphone, and iOS companion app to deliver live transcription, real-time translation across 60+ languages, hands-free AI assistance, and searchable memory of everyday conversations. Mira raised a $6.6M seed round led by General Catalyst and began shipping its first devices in January 2026. It is a privacy-first consumer wearable with an iOS companion app and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Spacetime Studios
providers.description: Spacetime Studios is an Austin, Texas mobile game developer and the creator of the free-to-play "Legends" series of cross-platform MMORPGs, including Arcane Legends, Pocket Legends, Star Legends, and Dark Legends. Founded by veteran game developers, the studio operates a consumer-facing community forum, an in-game item web store, and player support channels. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its verified public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: Improbable
providers.description: Improbable (Improbable Worlds Ltd) is a London-based technology company and venture builder. Founded in 2012, it originally built SpatialOS, a distributed simulation and networking platform for large-scale real-time multiplayer games, and later Morpheus / M² (MSquared), a network of interoperable metaverse worlds. Today Improbable operates primarily as a venture builder and capital allocator, partnering with founders to launch and scale companies across AI, Web3 and the metaverse. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and the SoftBank Vision Fund. Its historical developer surface centered on the SpatialOS Platform SDK, Worker SDK and the `spatial` CLI (distributed via NuGet), plus the improbable-eng and spatialos GitHub organizations; the standalone documentation, status and IMS subdomains have since been retired as the company pivoted away from a standalone developer platform.

providers.name: Tripledot
providers.description: Tripledot Studios (Tripledot Group) is a London-headquartered mobile games developer and publisher focused on data-driven casual games, with chart-topping titles including Woodoku, Solitaire, Duplica, Wordhop, Solitaire Scapes, Sudoku, Spider Solitaire and Blackjack played by more than 25 million daily active users. Founded as an independent studio and named Best Developer at the Pocket Gamer Mobile Games Awards 2023, Tripledot closed an $800 million acquisition of AppLovin's mobile games studio portfolio (ten studios) on July 1, 2025, and is backed by investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners. Tripledot publishes no first-party developer API, portal or SDKs, but its website ships a real llms.txt and a live, publicly connectable MCP endpoint (the Wix Site Visitor Assistant) for agentic access to site content.

providers.name: Playabl
providers.description: Playabl is a no-code, conversational game creation platform that lets anyone build games and interactive experiences by chatting with AI. Operated by Replkt, Inc. and backed by Y Combinator, Playabl turns natural-language prompts into playable games across genres including sports, idle, brainrot, dopamine, and think/puzzle categories, with no coding required. The product is a consumer-facing web application (playabl.ai); as of this profile Playabl does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Playsome
providers.description: Playsome (Playsome Ltd. / Playsome Oy) is a Helsinki, Finland mobile game studio that builds free-to-play games combining deep gameplay with polished visuals under the philosophy of making "big games with a small team". Its flagship title is Friends & Dragons, a cooperative multiplayer puzzle-RPG for iOS and Android featuring 150+ collectible heroes and 700+ puzzles and dungeons. The company is backed by gaming-focused venture firms Play Ventures and EQT. Playsome does not publish a traditional developer API, but its Wix-hosted website exposes a live Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic AI access, letting agents retrieve business details, search the site, and start bookings/purchases without scraping.

providers.name: Pop.in
providers.description: Pop.in is a consumer social gaming platform that connects people through real-time multiplayer games including Spades, Hearts, Dominoes, Liar's Dice, crosswords, Pop Quiz trivia, and Just Chatting. Delivered as iOS and Android apps plus a web play surface at play.pop.in, the service reports over 100M downloads and 20M active users with a 4.75+ average rating. The company is backed by 500 Global and was surfaced through its portfolio; it operates a purely consumer-facing product and publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: ThriveFantasy
providers.description: ThriveFantasy was a New York City daily fantasy sports platform focused on player-prop pick'em contests across NFL, NBA, MLB, esports, and other leagues, backed by Bullpen Capital. The company ceased operations in early 2024 after a failed funding round and a player-withdrawal crisis. It never published a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; its legacy marketing site remains online.

providers.name: Loftia
providers.description: Loftia is a cozy, solarpunk massively-multiplayer online (MMO) game developed by Qloud Games Pty Ltd, a remote-first indie studio founded in 2022 and headquartered in Sydney, Australia. Set across floating islands in a warm, sustainable world, players farm, craft, decorate, socialize, and build a life in the sky alongside friends in a shared world that grows over time. The studio (founded by Eric Mallon, Martina Qin, and Michael Su) raised a $5M seed round led by BITKRAFT Ventures and GFR Fund with participation from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and took part in a16z's SPEEDRUN gaming accelerator. Loftia is a consumer game company with no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: General Intuition
providers.description: General Intuition is a frontier AI lab, founded in 2025 and spun out of Medal, building spatial-temporal world and action models that learn to perceive, anticipate, and act in space and time. Rather than training primarily on the archive of human language, its systems learn from gameplay data, teaching machines to play, dream within compressed simulacra of reality, and improvise within the unfolding dynamics of the world. The company is developing a commercial API for gaming, simulation, and robotics partners, with broader access planned through 2026. General Intuition is backed by Khosla Ventures, which led both its $133.7M seed round (October 2025) and its $320M Series A at a $2.3B valuation (2026).

providers.name: Illumix
providers.description: Illumix is an enterprise-grade spatial AI company spun out of Stanford's Computer Science Department, providing a core stack for real-world location intelligence that runs at the edge with centimeter-level precision. Its hardware-agnostic platform delivers sub-second localization and 3D mapping across mobile devices, AR/VR wearables, and robotics using standard cameras — with no LiDAR or GPS dependency — combining multimodal vision-language AI with long-term memory that learns behavior over time. Illumix serves AI/XR wearables, enterprise and logistics, defense and security, location-based entertainment, and robotics, with deployments referenced for Disney, Six Flags, Cedar Fair, MGM Resorts, Warner Bros, Verizon, and Sony. The company markets developer APIs and an SDK as part of a full-stack offering, but publishes no public developer portal, reference documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Dream Games
providers.description: Dream Games is a mobile gaming company founded in 2019 with offices in Istanbul, Turkey and London, UK. It develops and publishes high-quality casual mobile games, most notably the match-three puzzle hit Royal Match and its follow-up Royal Kingdom. Royal Match became one of the top-grossing mobile games worldwide, and the company has raised multiple funding rounds reaching a multibillion-dollar valuation. Dream Games does not publish a public developer API or developer program; it is present in the API Evangelist network as a company profile enriched with its public identity, security, and domain artifacts.

providers.name: dreamgames
providers.description: Dream Games is a mobile gaming developer with offices in Istanbul and London that builds high-quality, long-lifecycle casual puzzle games, best known for Royal Match and Royal Kingdom. The company combines technology and creativity to produce polished match-3 titles played by tens of millions of players worldwide, and it was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital. Dream Games operates as a consumer game publisher rather than an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or programmatic API surface. This profile therefore captures the company's real public web, legal, and security surface (website, terms, privacy, careers, help center, and a published security.txt) rather than developer artifacts.

providers.name: Alta VR
providers.description: Alta VR (legally Another Axiom LLC) is a virtual reality game studio behind Gorilla Tag, one of the most-played VR titles ever, and the newer social VR world Orion Drift. The studio builds imaginative, physics-driven multiplayer experiences centered on hand-based locomotion and social play across Meta Quest, Steam, and other VR platforms. It runs an Another Axiom Creator Program for community map-building and content creation, and publishes game code and Unity map-export tooling through its public GitHub organization. Alta VR is a portfolio company of a16z. As a VR consumer game studio it does not currently operate a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program; its developer-facing surface is limited to open-source game code, custom map tooling, and creator resources.

providers.name: Antimatter Systems
providers.description: Antimatter Systems is an education technology company building a peer-to-peer learning network where students demonstrate mastery by making memes, puzzles, and games rather than by writing essays or sitting tests. Founded by Jonathan Libov, the company raised a $2M seed round led by Version One Ventures in 2023, joined by Spacecadet, Ordinary Holdings, Haystack and Compound. Its classroom product lets teachers create meme-based activities with deadlines and instructions, invite students by shareable link, moderate submissions, restrict learners to view-only, work from a library of pre-approved templates, catch unedited-image uploads with plagiarism detection, and grade every submission in one place; the company states it should be free for schools. Antimatter also ships a Sorcerer AI instructional coach plus the consumer Antimatter: Creator and Antimatter: Universe iOS apps. The platform runs on the web at playantimatter.com. As of July 2026 the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Draftea
providers.description: Draftea is a Mexico-based daily fantasy sports and real-money sports gaming platform, billed as the first daily fantasy sports (DFS) product for the Spanish-speaking world. Fans draft lineups of real athletes across soccer, American football (via an NFL partnership), basketball, baseball, and Formula 1, enter paid contests, and compete against other users for cash prizes rather than against a bookmaker. The company operates in Mexico under regulatory approval (DGAJS/SCEVF/P-06/2005-TER), distributes through native iOS and Android apps, and is backed by Sequoia, Kaszek, Bullpen Capital, Stepstone Group, and Courtside Ventures, along with athlete investors. Draftea is a consumer product company and does not currently publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its public web, support, legal, and open-source engineering surface.

providers.name: Dream11
providers.description: Dream11 is India's largest fantasy sports platform, operated by Sporta Technologies Private Limited and part of the Dream Sports group founded in 2008 by Harsh Jain and Bhavit Sheth and headquartered in Mumbai. Launched as a freemium fantasy game in 2012, it lets 140 million-plus users draft virtual teams and compete in free and paid contests across cricket, football, kabaddi, basketball and hockey, scoring on the real-world performance of the athletes they pick. Dream11 is a consumer, mobile-first product with no public consumer API program; its engineering organization does maintain public open-source infrastructure (Kong rate-limiter and circuit-breaker plugins, the Odin deployment tool) on GitHub and publishes an engineering blog.

providers.name: InfiniGods
providers.description: InfiniGods is a gaming studio building fun, free-to-play, Web3-powered mobile games centered around ancient mythologies. Its titles — Immortal Siege, King of Destiny, and InfiniMerge — share interoperable gaming assets, items, power-ups, and currencies that span the InfiniGods Universe (IGU). Players collect blockchain assets such as the Elder Gods (a 4,488-piece Gen 0 NFT collection that unlocks abilities and boosts scoring across all titles) and the InfiniPass VIP membership (early access, bonus play, exclusive NFT drops, and in-game boosts). The company is backed by Pantera Capital. InfiniGods is a consumer game studio with no public developer/API program; this profile captures its public web, legal, community, and code-org surface.

providers.name: Yield Guild Games
providers.description: Yield Guild Games (YGG) is a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) and one of the world's first and largest web3 gaming guilds, founded in 2020 by Gabby Dizon, Beryl Li, and the pseudonymous "Owl of Moistness" out of the Philippines. YGG invests in NFTs and blockchain-game assets, lends them to players, and shares the resulting yield with its community and YGG token holders. Its onchain Guild Protocol (launched on Base) equips guilds with a modular library of smart-contract tooling for treasury wallets, programmable quests, and contribution tracking, while YGG Play acts as a publisher for casual crypto games. The company was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), which led a $4.6M round in 2021. Note: this repository slug "yield-guide-games" preserves an upstream typo of the real company name, Yield Guild Games.

providers.name: ForeVR
providers.description: ForeVR Games is a consumer virtual-reality game studio that brings classic social bar and backyard games into VR. Its catalog includes ForeVR Bowl, ForeVR Darts, ForeVR Pool, and ForeVR Cornhole, built for multiplayer play across Meta Quest, Steam VR, and PlayStation VR2. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. ForeVR is a consumer game publisher with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Wooga
providers.description: Wooga is a Berlin-based mobile game developer founded in 2009 and a subsidiary of Playtika, specializing in story-driven casual games such as June's Journey, Ghost Detective and Pearl's Peril. Wooga publishes no public API or developer portal, but maintains an active open-source GitHub organization with its atlas Gradle plugin suite for Unity and mobile build automation, published to the Gradle Plugin Portal and RubyGems. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and hv-capital.

providers.name: Crystal Dynamics
providers.description: Crystal Dynamics is a AAA video game development studio, best known as the home of the Tomb Raider franchise and its Lara Croft character, and part of the Embracer Group. The studio publishes a consumer-facing marketing website, careers portal, player support center, and news/community hub, but exposes no public developer API program, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio stub lead; enrichment confirms there is no public API surface to catalog at this time.

providers.name: Ergatta
providers.description: Ergatta is a connected-fitness company that makes game-based home rowing machines, pairing WaterRower-derived water-resistance hardware handcrafted in Rhode Island with a gamified software platform of interactive challenges (Endeavor, Meteor, Wavelength), live and on-demand races, scenic rows, coached classes, and custom workouts. Ergatta sells the Luxe and Lite rowers plus upgrade kits for existing WaterRower and Concept2 machines, delivered through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront with a membership subscription. Ergatta does not publish a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web surface and identity for network discovery.

providers.name: Hutch Games
providers.description: Hutch Games (Hutch) is a mobile game development studio founded in London with additional studios in Dundee, Scotland and Nova Scotia, Canada. Hutch specializes in free-to-play mobile driving and car games, developing and publishing titles including F1 Clash, Top Drives, and Matchcreek Motors. The studio was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer mobile game publisher, Hutch does not currently expose a public developer API or developer program; this profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Jackpocket
providers.description: Jackpocket is a third-party lottery courier and mobile app that lets users in supported US states order official state lottery tickets — Powerball, Mega Millions, and regional draw games — from their phone, with the physical tickets stored securely on their behalf and winnings paid out through the app. Founded in 2013 in New York City by Peter Sullivan, the company was acquired by DraftKings in 2024. Jackpocket is a consumer-facing gaming/lottery brand; it does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or webhook surface. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a network entity with its public web properties and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Kabam
providers.description: Kabam is a mobile game developer and publisher founded in 2006 and headquartered in Vancouver, Canada, operating as a wholly owned subsidiary of Netmarble. The studio builds free-to-play multiplayer titles for iOS and Android, best known for Marvel Contest of Champions, alongside Shop Titans, Transformers Forged to Fight, King Arthur Legends, and past titles such as Disney Mirrorverse and Fast & Furious games. Kabam operates studios and offices across Vancouver, Montreal, Charlottetown, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Austin, and Seoul. Kabam publishes no public developer program, API reference, or SDK surface; this profile captures its public web, legal, and support properties plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Lil Snack
providers.description: Lil Snack is a Manhattan Beach, California games company, founded in 2024, that builds "snackable" daily games and party games — short pop-culture puzzle, word, and trivia titles that refresh every day. It runs its own consumer destination at lilsnack.com (Clue Daily, Scattergories Daily, Swap, DownWords, Pickle, Lite Brite Daily, Wheel of Fortune TODAY, Quiz Climb, Venn, Chain, and more) and also powers games embedded inside partner consumer platforms, citing BuzzFeed, FOX, Hasbro, the Los Angeles Times, Netflix, Peacock, Prime Gaming, Reddit, and Sony. The company reports 40M+ games played and 10M+ players all-time, and monetizes through platform partnerships, sponsorships, and brand licensing. As of this profile Lil Snack publishes NO public developer surface — no API, no documentation portal, no SDKs, no public GitHub organization, and no /.well-known documents; its partner game integrations are arranged through business development rather than self-serve APIs. This API Evangelist profile therefore captures verified company identity, web properties, and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Odyssey Interactive
providers.description: Odyssey Interactive is an independent game development studio focused on building free-to-play, cross-platform, competitive titles set in bright, hopeful, anime-inspired IP. The studio is best known for Omega Strikers, a free-to-play competitive arena game, and its mission is to "ignite the spark of competitiveness that lives within everyone" by creating community-driven games with longevity. Odyssey Interactive was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal — its public surface is its marketing site, a Verified Creators program, downloadable game asset kits, and a Zendesk-hosted player support center. This profile captures the studio's identity and verified public links.

providers.name: Peak
providers.description: Peak is a consumer brain-training mobile application operated by Synaptic Labs (formerly Peak Labs) that offers cognitive exercise games and personalized workouts spanning memory, attention, problem-solving, mental agility, language, and emotion. Its games and Advanced Training Programmes are developed with researchers from institutions including Cambridge, Yale, UCL, and King's College London. Peak Pro is a subscription that unlocks 40+ games, personalized workouts, performance analytics, and an AI Coach. Peak is a mobile-only consumer product distributed via the App Store and Google Play and does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Pokelabo
providers.description: Pokelabo (ポケラボ) is a Japanese mobile game development studio founded in 2007 and headquartered in Tokyo. Originally an independent social-game maker, it became a subsidiary of GREE and, as of January 1, 2025, was integrated into WFS (Wright Flyer Studios) under the GREE group. The studio develops and operates smartphone games built on licensed and original intellectual properties, including titles such as SINoALICE and Magia Exedra (Puella Magi Madoka Magica). Pokelabo is a consumer entertainment company and does not expose a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Poker Skill
providers.description: Poker Skill is a mobile-first poker-training app for iOS and Android that turns learning poker into a daily habit. It teaches through interactive puzzles, bite-sized guided lessons, and daily practice reps that adapt to the player's skill level, from complete beginner to serious improver. At its core is "Showdown AI", a versioned game-theory engine that deals practice hands, plays the opponents, and grades every decision by its expected value — an approach the company says replicates the methods behind Pluribus, the first AI to beat top professionals at six-max no-limit hold'em. The product is subscription-funded with a free-to-start funnel, and is backed by Initialized Capital. Poker Skill is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: PortalOne
providers.description: PortalOne is a hybrid gaming platform that blends mobile games with live, interactive television-style entertainment, letting players compete inside shows and classic titles such as Atari's Breakout. Operated by PortalOne AS (Norway) and PortalOne, Inc. (United States), the company delivers its experience through native iOS and Android apps rather than a public developer platform. It is a consumer-facing entertainment product backed by Seedcamp and other venture investors; as of this profile PortalOne publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Quago Technologies LTD
providers.description: Quago Technologies is a gaming analytics and fraud-detection company that uses machine learning and mobile device sensor data to protect and optimize mobile games. Its platform analyzes in-game behavioral and device-sensor patterns - without collecting personally identifiable information - to detect and manage cheating, identify user-acquisition (CPA) fraud, predict player churn, and optimize monetization and lifetime value. Quago is delivered to mobile game studios as an embedded SDK plus a backend analytics service rather than a public developer API; it was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Resolution Games
providers.description: Resolution Games is a Stockholm-based studio building games for virtual, augmented, and mixed reality platforms including Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro, and PlayStation VR. Its titles include Demeo, Spatial Ops, Blaston, Bait!, and Ultimechs. The company is venture-backed (Creandum, GV, Partech) and runs a consumer-facing games business. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public web properties (blog, support, legal pages) for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Sandbox VR
providers.description: Sandbox VR is a location-based virtual reality entertainment company operating full-body, free-roam VR experiences for groups of friends, families, and corporate teams across 60+ venues in North America, Europe, and Asia. Guests play social, multiplayer VR adventures — horror, action, sports, and family-friendly titles including licensed properties — using motion-tracked suits and headsets. The business spans company-owned and franchised locations, online booking, gift cards, parties/events, and an unlimited-pass subscription. Backed by a16z and Craft Ventures. Sandbox VR is a consumer entertainment operator and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this record captures the company identity and its public web/security posture.

providers.name: Splash
providers.description: Splash is an AI music-creation platform building games and tools for a new generation of creators. Developed by the team formerly known as Popgun AI, it has built proprietary generative-audio technology and high-quality music datasets since 2017, powering features such as Text-to-Singing, Text-to-Rap, and Generative Text-to-Music. Splash's consumer products include the Splash beat-maker app for iOS and Android, SPLASH on Roblox, the WeMix collaborative music experience, and KAIMIX. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures, Techstars, the Alexa Fund, Bitkraft, King River Capital, and Mawson. Splash publishes no public developer API or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its public web identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Summoners Arena
providers.description: Summoners Arena is a blockchain-based, multi-genre play-to-earn game universe set in the antique lore of Summonia, where players summon, evolve, and battle NFT heroes across PvP modes (Arena, Battleground) and PvE content (Dungeon, Campaign), with an in-game NFT marketplace supporting hero renting, equipment collection, and forging. Backed by Pantera Capital, it operates in the Web3 / crypto gaming sector. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes a consumer game and community surface but no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or well-known discovery documents were found.

providers.name: Super Evil
providers.description: Super Evil (Super Evil Megacorp) is an award-winning independent video game studio building shared, cross-platform gaming experiences that push creative and technical boundaries. The studio is best known for the MOBA Vainglory and the shooter Catalyst Black, and has shipped licensed titles including TMNT: Splintered Fate and a Rebel Moon game (Blood Line). Surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes only a consumer marketing website (Gatsby/Netlify) and social channels; it exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, OpenAPI, developer portal, or status page.

providers.name: Super Evil Megacorp
providers.description: Super Evil Megacorp is an award-winning independent video game studio building shared, cross-platform gaming experiences that push creative and technical boundaries. Founded in 2012, the studio is best known for the mobile MOBA Vainglory and has since shipped titles including Catalyst Black, TMNT Splintered Fate, and Blood Line - Rebel Moon, developed on its own in-house game engine. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Index Ventures; it is a consumer games studio and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Tactile Games
providers.description: Tactile Games is a Danish mobile game studio headquartered in Copenhagen, founded in 2014, that builds and publishes casual free-to-play puzzle titles for iOS and Android. Its portfolio includes Lily's Garden, Penny & Flo, Makeover Match, the Cookie Cats series (Cookie Cats, Cookie Cats Pop, Cookie Cats Blast), and the Simon's Cat games. Tactile is a portfolio company of Index Ventures. It is a consumer game publisher rather than an API producer: it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain-security posture surfaced by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Vivid Vision
providers.description: Vivid Vision is a digital vision care company that builds VR- and software-based tools for diagnosing and treating binocular vision disorders. Its products include a vision training system for amblyopia (lazy eye), strabismus, and convergence insufficiency; Vivid Vision Perimetry (VVP), a VR-based visual field test used as an endpoint in ophthalmology clinical trials for geographic atrophy, AMD, and glaucoma; and EYEBAB VT therapeutic exercises for clinical settings. Founded in 2014, the platform has been used by more than 100,000 patients across 50+ countries through eye-care practices and clinics. Vivid Vision is backed by Uncork Capital. The company is a patient- and clinician-facing vision-care provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: Voldex
providers.description: Voldex (Voldex Entertainment) is a game developer and publisher founded in 2015 that acquires, operates, and grows platform-leading games on Roblox, including Brookhaven, Driving Empire, and NFL Universe Football, collectively reaching over 140 million monthly players. Its stated mission is to "bring people together through fun," pursuing a focused strategy of selectively acquiring and stewarding enduring Roblox experiences rather than broad portfolio expansion. Voldex publishes no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or API documentation surface — it is a consumer games studio whose products run inside the Roblox platform. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; it was reviewed by the enrichment pipeline and confirmed to have no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Volley
providers.description: Volley is a San Francisco voice-AI entertainment company, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, that builds voice-controlled and connected-TV games. Its catalog includes hits such as Song Quiz, Yes Sire, and officially licensed titles like Jeopardy!, Wheel of Fortune, and Family Feud, playable on Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Roku, Fire TV, LG, and Samsung TVs. The company is rebranding its consumer surface as "Weekend." Volley operates as a consumer entertainment product studio and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: World Golf Tour
providers.description: World Golf Tour (WGT Golf), operated by World Golf Tour, LLC out of San Francisco, is a free-to-play online golf simulation launched in 2008 that recreates more than twenty real championship courses like Pebble Beach, St Andrews, and Bethpage Black using photorealistic imagery, played by over 15 million players on web, iOS, and Android, with virtual equipment from Callaway, Titleist, and TaylorMade and integrations with SkyTrak launch monitors. The company is a Battery Ventures portfolio company and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Lilith Games
providers.description: Lilith Games (上海莉莉丝网络科技有限公司) is a Shanghai-headquartered video game developer and publisher founded in 2013, known for globally distributed mobile and PC titles including Rise of Kingdoms (万国觉醒), AFK Arena (剑与远征), AFK Journey (剑与远征：启程), Farlight 84 (远光84), Warpath (战火勋章), Art of Conquest (剑与家园) and a portfolio of indie games. The company operates as a consumer game publisher rather than an API platform: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or partner API program. Its public engineering surface is the LilithGames GitHub organization, which open-sources backend and build infrastructure (Go networking and reverse-proxy tooling, build caching, Perforce virtual file system work) rather than client SDKs for a Lilith API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital.

providers.name: Ubiquity6
providers.description: Ubiquity6 was a San Francisco augmented-reality startup ("Capture & Edit Reality") backed by Benchmark, First Round, and Index Ventures. It built Display.land, a multiplayer 3D/AR/VR capture and creation platform, acquired Wavy AR, and was acquired by Discord in June 2021, after which its products were discontinued. Ubiquity6 never published a public API or developer program; its GitHub organization survives as a set of open-source computer vision and React Native forks, and a few internal packages remain on npm under the @ubiquity6 scope.

providers.name: Five Jack
providers.description: Five Jack (PT. Five Jack) is the Indonesian company behind itemku, one of Southeast Asia's largest digital-goods marketplaces for gamers. Founded in 2014 as a game price-comparison and classifieds platform, itemku grew into a full marketplace where buyers and sellers trade in-game items, currency, account top-ups, game keys, and vouchers across 200+ game categories including Roblox, Genshin Impact, Mobile Legends, Dota 2, Steam, and Growtopia. The company reached one million orders in 2018, launched its Android app and gaming blog in 2020, and became part of Bukalapak (IDX: BUKA) in May 2021. Five Jack was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It operates a consumer-facing marketplace and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: 1047 Games
providers.description: 1047 Games is an independent video game studio best known for the arena shooter Splitgate and its follow-up title EMPULSE, a free-to-play movement shooter. Backed by Insight Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners, the studio ships games across PC (Steam), PlayStation, and Xbox. As a consumer game publisher it exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks its public web, legal, and community surfaces for the API Evangelist network. Added originally as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with live domain-security and identity probes.

providers.name: 8th Wall
providers.description: 8th Wall is a web-based augmented reality (WebAR) platform originally founded in 2016 and acquired by Niantic in March 2022. Following Niantic's 2025 sale of its gaming division to Scopely and the spin-off of Niantic Spatial, Inc. as an independent geospatial AI and XR company, 8th Wall's hosted cloud editor, login, and Niantic Studio services were retired on February 28, 2026 and the platform transitioned to a free, open-source distribution model. Existing published 8th Wall experiences continue to run through February 28, 2027. The 8th Wall stack centers on the XR Engine — a SLAM-based WebAR runtime providing World Tracking, Image Targets, Face Effects, Sky Segmentation, and World Effects — exposed to developers as a TypeScript/JavaScript SDK that integrates with A-Frame, three.js, PlayCanvas, and Babylon.js. The Distributed Engine Binary (released January 2026) ships SLAM under a binary-only license for commercial and noncommercial use, while the surrounding framework, utilities, and example projects are MIT-licensed on the 8thwall GitHub organization. 8th Wall Studio (formerly Niantic Studio) is a real-time visual editor and game engine for authoring 3D and XR experiences that can be deployed to any web host. 8th Wall does not publish a public REST or HTTP API; the developer surface is a client-side JavaScript SDK plus command-line and utility tooling distributed through GitHub.

providers.name: B612
providers.description: B612 is a consumer selfie and beauty camera application for iOS and Android, published globally by SNOW Corporation and operated in mainland China as B612咔叽 (B612 Kaji) by Yiruike Information Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. The app combines a real-time beauty camera, AR stickers and scene effects, user-created and creator-published filters, and photo and video editing tools, and has been distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play since 2014. B612 is a mobile end-user product rather than an API provider: as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer portal, no public API documentation, no SDKs, and no machine-readable API artifacts on any of its web properties.

providers.name: FreshPlanet
providers.description: FreshPlanet Inc. is a New York City based mobile game developer, headquartered at 200 Hudson St, New York, NY 10013, best known for the music trivia franchise SongPop. The studio builds free-to-play mobile entertainment titles for iOS and Android, combining licensed music catalogs, social multiplayer play, and live events. FreshPlanet is a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. As a consumer game studio it does not operate a public developer program or API: it exposes only a marketing site, player support via a Zendesk help center, and standard legal surfaces (Terms of Use and Privacy Policy). This profile captures the studio's real public web and legal footprint for the API Evangelist network; there is no OpenAPI, SDK, or agent surface to enrich because the company publishes none.

providers.name: Funcom
providers.description: Funcom is a Norwegian video-game developer and publisher founded in 1993, headquartered in Oslo with additional studios in Raleigh (North Carolina), Lisbon, and Bucharest. It is best known for online, open-world, and survival titles including Dune: Awakening, Conan Exiles, Age of Conan, and The Secret World / Secret World Legends, alongside published titles such as Metal: Hellsinger, Aloft, Dune: Spice Wars, and Mutant Year Zero. Funcom is majority-owned by Tencent. It was surfaced as a Northzone portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer API surface, so this profile captures company identity, legal/support links, and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Futureplay
providers.description: Futureplay is a Helsinki, Finland-based mobile game studio founded in 2015 that develops free-to-play games for a global audience, having released six titles for more than 120 million players including Merge Gardens, Battlelands Royale, and Idle Farming Empire. Backed by Creandum and now part of Plarium, the studio operates in the consumer gaming sector. Futureplay publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal; player-facing support runs through a Zendesk help center, and legal terms are hosted on the Plarium company site.

providers.name: Geopipe
providers.description: Geopipe uses AI and machine learning to build game-ready digital twins of real-world cities and environments. It ingests raw sensor data (imagery and laser scans) and reconstructs regions as semantically-modeled, multi-level-of- detail 3D models that developers stream or download into games, simulations, training, architecture, and metaverse applications without any manual 3D modeling. Delivery is through Cesium 3D Tiles streaming for Unity and Unreal Engine, downloadable 3D meshes in common file formats, ready-to-use Unity Asset Store packs, and a first-party Unity SDK, backed by an open-source geospatial and 3D-tiles toolchain on GitHub. Founded in New York City by Christopher Mitchell and Thomas Dickerson and backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Gym Class VR
providers.description: Gym Class VR (operating as "Gym Class" by IRL Studios) is a social virtual reality sports gaming platform for Meta Quest headsets and mobile devices, offering multiplayer basketball, baseball, football, boxing, paintball, and soccer experiences where players compete, socialize, and create and share their own games. The top-rated sports title on the Meta Quest Store with a 4.8-star average across 53,000+ ratings, the company holds licensing agreements with the NBA and Major League Baseball, expanded to mobile in 2026, and has raised over $8M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Y Combinator, and NBA players. It is a consumer VR entertainment product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Immersive Gamebox
providers.description: Immersive Gamebox is a London-founded (2018) location-based entertainment company operating indoor gaming venues across the UK, US, Germany, and the UAE. Each Gamebox combines projection mapping, touch screens, motion tracking, and surround sound to deliver fully immersive, interactive games for teams of two to six players in 30-60 minute sessions. Its catalog spans licensed titles built with partners such as Netflix (Squid Game), Aardman (Shaun the Sheep), Rovio (Angry Birds), and Tetris, alongside originals, and the business runs on bookings, party and corporate packages, Game Pass subscriptions, and a multi-unit franchise model. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of index-ventures. It exposes no public web/REST API today; developer collaboration is limited to a Unity-based SDK offered to game studios building titles for the Gamebox hardware platform.

providers.name: Junglee Games
providers.description: Junglee Games is a skill-based online gaming company founded in 2012 by Ankush Gera, operating as an independent subsidiary of Flutter Entertainment, which acquired a majority stake in 2021 in a deal valuing the company at more than $440 million. Headquartered in Gurugram with a studio in Bengaluru, the company builds and operates consumer real-money and casual gaming apps for a base of over 150 million users, with flagship titles including Junglee Rummy, the Howzat fantasy cricket and football platform, Carrom Stars, and Junglee Poker. The company positions trust, safety, and fairness as engineering priorities. Junglee Games is a consumer gaming provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documented API program; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and probed security posture for the API Evangelist network. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: mojiworks
providers.description: Mojiworks is a UK-based social games studio, backed by Balderton Capital, that is pioneering a game genre it calls MuGC (Multi-User Generative Creation) — living, collaborative worlds that communities and AI systems build together. Its released titles include Ready Chef Go, Trivia Party, Chef Showdown and Hatch Cats, and it is building its first MuGC world as a persistent, community-shaped city. The company publishes a public AI Ethics Policy committing to licensed training data, environmental accountability, human oversight and content-safety controls. Mojiworks does not currently expose a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record and enrichment lead.

providers.name: Osmo
providers.description: Osmo (Tangible Play) makes hands-on, screen-interactive learning games for iPad and Fire tablet that pair a physical reflector base placed over the device camera with digital games spanning math, coding, spelling, drawing, and problem-solving for children. Backed by Accel and GV, Osmo is a consumer educational-technology brand that sells hardware kits and companion apps direct to families and schools. As of this enrichment pass it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Phoenix Labs
providers.description: Phoenix Labs is an independent video game developer with studios in Vancouver and Montreal, building immersive online worlds and community-driven games. Its titles include the free-to-play action RPG Dauntless and the cozy life-sim Fae Farm. The studio operates player-facing support and account services for its games but does not publish a public developer platform, API program, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Sapphire Ventures and enriched into the API Evangelist network; its API surface is currently none.

providers.name: PlayQ
providers.description: PlayQ is a Los Angeles-based mobile game developer and publisher creating free-to-play games for a global audience, including titles such as Charm King and Treasure Party. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network.
