As of this enrichment pass PlayQ operates a consumer-facing marketing and game-support website with no public developer portal, API documentation, or API surface; player support is routed through per-game Zendesk help centers.

providers.name: Pops
providers.description: Pops is a consumer mobile application, built by Undefined Software, Inc. and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), that lets users create, remix, and share AI-powered mini games with friends. Every play instantly becomes a funny gameplay/reaction video you can send to friends. Pops is available on iOS and Android and is organized around game categories such as arcade, 3D, racing, sports, puzzles, party, and reaction games. It is an end-user social and gaming product with no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: RealNetworks
providers.description: RealNetworks is a Seattle-based technology company that pairs AI-powered computer-vision and secure-communication products with its long-running consumer media brands. Its portfolio includes SAFR (facial recognition for security and retail loss prevention), Kontxt (AI messaging and voice security for CPaaS platforms, Telcos, and MNOs), GameHouse (cross-device casual gaming), and RealPlayer (media playback). Product APIs for SAFR and Kontxt are delivered through authenticated partner portals rather than an open developer portal; the historical Real Developer Program (developer.real.com) is no longer live, and no public OpenAPI specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Supersolid
providers.description: Supersolid is a London, UK based mobile game developer and publisher, backed by Index Ventures, that designs and operates free-to-play mobile titles across merge, cooking, simulation, and multiplayer arena genres. Its portfolio includes Cook & Merge, Snake Rivals, Home Street, Food Street, Adventure Town, Super Penguins, and RoPets. Supersolid is a consumer-facing games studio and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web properties (support, careers, terms, privacy) and domain-security posture. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures.

providers.name: tagSpace
providers.description: tagSpace is a Spatial AI platform, part of the tagStorm group, that lets creators and brands publish interactive augmented-reality experiences and spatial content anchored to real-world places. Through its create, explore, and publish surfaces, tagSpace offers a creator-economy platform where makers showcase spatial "tags," and its tagAI layer applies AI to spatial content. It markets to brands and enterprises (B2B) with named partners including RTL, Telekom, Telstra, Warner Music Group and others. The public site is a Framer marketing presence; as of this enrichment pass tagSpace exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or well-known API metadata. This profile remains an identity-only company record.

providers.name: TaleMonster Games
providers.description: TaleMonster Games is a fully remote mobile game studio whose mission is to create games that surprise, challenge, and evolve with players. The team is united by a shared obsession for product craft and a deep love for games, and ships casual mobile titles to iOS and Android. Its debut title, Match Valley, is a casual match puzzle game published on the Apple App Store and Google Play. TaleMonster Games publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or technical documentation; this profile captures its public company and product identity.

providers.name: Talofa Games
providers.description: Talofa Games is a mobile game developer and publisher backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The studio builds social fitness games that turn real-world physical activity into cooperative multiplayer play. Its flagship title, Run Legends, is a free-to-play running RPG available on iOS and Android in which players' real-world runs and walks power team battles against monsters, and its newer title Monster Walk is in closed beta. Talofa Games is a consumer mobile-gaming company and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile captures its company identity and public web presence rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Triumph Arcade
providers.description: Triumph Labs (originally Triumph Arcade) is a consumer entertainment and commerce company that builds mobile apps for competitive, skill-based gaming and collectibles. Its flagship products are Triumph: Play for Cash, a real-money skill-gaming platform, and Rips by Triumph, a live collectibles and trading-card ripping experience. Backed by Multicoin Capital, the company operates consumer iOS apps and publishes no public developer API surface; this profile tracks the company identity, legal, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Upsight
providers.description: Upsight was a mobile analytics and marketing platform for apps and games — positioning itself as a "user lifecycle management platform" combining omnichannel analytics, integrated web and mobile marketing, ad optimization, and a DataMine SQL analytics product behind a single SDK for iOS, Android, tvOS, Unity, and Web. A Battery Ventures portfolio company, the platform is now defunct - upsight.com no longer resolves, the help.upsight.com developer docs survive only in the Internet Archive, and the GitHub org has been dormant since 2020, though the UpsightKit CocoaPods SDK and the doctor PyPI package remain published.

providers.name: videogame.ai
providers.description: videogame.ai is an AI-native game development studio that uses fleets of autonomous AI coding agents to build, ship, and operate video games. The company offers full-service game development delivered in days at the cost of a single full-time employee, along with automated live-ops pipelines, a multiplayer engine optimized for AI coding agents, an AI-native asset and media management system, and autonomous generation of ads and creative from game builds. Featured titles include Zero Hour, a narrative game set on a frozen planet, and Imperfect World, an RPG built around time-loop mechanics. Backed by a16z (SR02) and Konvoy. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the studio publishes a marketing site and contact channel but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation at this time.

providers.name: AltspaceVR
providers.description: AltspaceVR was a social virtual reality platform founded in 2013 where people gathered in shared 3D spaces for live events, meetups, classes, comedy shows and conferences. Google Ventures (GV) was an early investor. Microsoft acquired the company in 2017 and folded it into its Mixed Reality division, then announced in January 2023 that the platform would close, shutting it down permanently on 2023-03-10 in favor of Microsoft Mesh. AltspaceVR published no hosted HTTP API; its developer surface was the Mixed Reality Extension (MRE) SDK for building server-hosted 3D world extensions in Node.js, plus the earlier web-based AltspaceSDK. Every SDK repository is now archived and altvr.com redirects to microsoft.com. This profile is retained as a historical record of a terminated platform, not as a live integration target.

providers.name: Endless Studios LLC
providers.description: Endless Studios LLC is a game development learning platform where aspiring creators learn to build video games through real, pro-studio projects. Its Endstar game engine lets creators code and collaborate in real time, while structured programs (Launchpad for beginners, Capstone for advanced participants) pair learners with 30+ game-industry mentors, expert playtesting, and collaborator matching across design, art, and programming. Learners build portfolios of shipped games to show potential employers. The company runs university, government, and partner programs (including a UAE national game-making competition) and is a 500 Global portfolio company. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public developer/API surface was found during enrichment (consumer/creator-facing product on the studio.endlessstudios.com app).

providers.name: Riiico
providers.description: RIIICO is a Duesseldorf-based industrial software company building 3D-AI tools that digitalize the factory shop floor. Its platform turns reality scans (point clouds) of existing plants into CAD-ready, pre-classified 3D models, cutting 3D modeling time by up to 80% and accelerating factory retrofit, robot programming, and simulation. RIIICO integrates with NVIDIA Omniverse (OpenUSD) and Siemens Xcelerator, and counts Siemens, Volvo, and Schaeffler among its customers. It won the Siemens Inventors of the Year Award 2024 and is backed by Earlybird, PiLabs, and seed + speed. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Talofa
providers.description: Talofa Games is a consumer mobile game studio, backed by Insight Partners, that builds location-based and fitness-driven games where real-world movement powers play. Its titles include Run Legends, a cooperative running RPG for iOS and Android in which players' real-world runs and steps fuel monster battles, and Monster Walk, a walking game currently in closed beta. The company distributes through the Apple App Store and Google Play and runs its community on Discord. As a consumer game publisher it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company with no API footprint.

providers.name: Animoca Brands
providers.description: Animoca Brands is a Web3 company focused on advancing digital property rights and building the open metaverse through blockchain technology, gaming, and digital assets. Founded in Hong Kong, the company operates a portfolio of consumer products including The Sandbox, Moca Network (digital identity), Open Campus (education), and Anichess, alongside institutional offerings such as Anchorpoint Financial (stablecoins and real-world assets) and NUVA (treasury management). Animoca Brands is also one of the most active investors in Web3, backing 600+ builders across gaming, infrastructure, real-world assets, and digital-ownership platforms. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network; Animoca operates primarily as a holding and investment company and does not publish a first-party public developer API.

providers.name: Azra Games
providers.description: Azra Games is a mobile role-playing game studio founded in 2022 by Mark Otero and headquartered in Sacramento, California. The studio builds RPGs on its proprietary "RPG GameKit" technology, with its flagship title UnGodly, a dark sword-and-sorcery RPG. Azra Games is backed by a16z and Pantera Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a game studio it publishes a public website, news, careers, terms, and privacy pages but does not expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Harmonix
providers.description: Harmonix Music Systems is one of the world's leading independent game development studios, best known for creating blockbuster music and rhythm franchises including Rock Band and Dance Central, alongside titles such as Amplitude, Fuser, DropMix, Audica, Super Beat Sports, and Harmonix Music VR. Founded in 1995 and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the studio was acquired by Epic Games in 2021 and continues to invent the future of music and motion gaming. Harmonix operates a consumer-facing web presence (games, music, community, blog, and press) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Roboto Games
providers.description: Roboto Games is an independent video game development studio building Stormforge, an open-world survival crafting game where players craft, build, fight, and harness epic storms to survive in a magical fantasy world. The studio was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a consumer game studio, Roboto Games publishes a marketing website, a careers page, and a studio blog, but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface — its player-facing experience is delivered through native game clients (Steam) and community channels (Discord, YouTube, Twitch) rather than an HTTP API. This profile captures the studio's public identity and web properties; no API artifacts are produced because none are published.

providers.name: Rovio Entertainment
providers.description: Rovio Entertainment is a Finnish mobile game company founded in 2003 and headquartered in Espoo, best known for the Angry Birds franchise and a portfolio of casual and puzzle titles played by hundreds of millions of players worldwide. It operates game studios across Finland, Sweden, Denmark, Canada, Spain, and Turkey, and became part of Sega Sammy Holdings in 2023. Rovio was surfaced as a portfolio company of Atomico and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Rovio publishes a corporate/marketing website but no public developer portal, API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Sett AI
providers.description: Sett AI is a creative performance AI platform for mobile game user acquisition (UA), offering "agentic AI" that helps game studios and performance-marketing teams research, generate, analyze, and deploy video and playable ad creatives at scale to combat creative fatigue. Sett agents connect to ad networks (Meta, Google, AppLovin, Unity, Mintegral) and MMP data to ideate concepts, generate playables and videos, and analyze creative performance. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners; the company raised a Series B bringing total funding to $57M. Sett operates a marketing and product website but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this profiling.

providers.name: Tyffon
providers.description: Tyffon Inc. is a Japanese immersive entertainment company that combines creativity and technology to deliver memorable XR experiences. The studio builds VR, AR, and mixed-reality attractions - including Corridor, Kaiju Haven VR, Floria, and Island Mirrorge MR - operates the Tyffonium attraction brand, licenses its XR content to entertainment venues across Japan, and released the GARA AR platform app. A Techstars portfolio company, Tyffon publishes no public developer portal or API surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Wildlife Studios
providers.description: Wildlife Studios is one of the world's largest mobile game developers and publishers, founded in Brazil in 2011. It builds and operates free-to-play games played globally, with more than 4.7 billion downloads across a portfolio of over 60 titles including Zooba, Sniper 3D, Tennis Clash, War Machines, and Sky Warriors, and runs a publishing division for third-party studios. Wildlife is a consumer gaming company: its public surface is player-facing games and corporate/careers content, not a developer platform. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP server. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and tracked in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Edge Markets
providers.description: EDGE Markets builds financial infrastructure for high-throughput gaming and trading environments, positioning itself as the "financial backbone for a new asset class." Its product line spans EDGE Boost, a high-limit debit platform (up to a $1,000,000 daily limit) with built-in responsible-gaming controls and activity tracking; EDGE Connect, a private payment rail and closed-loop settlement layer that replaces traditional consumer card networks to cut transaction costs and chargebacks; and EDGE Pro, a banking platform (in development) for market makers and institutional investors. The company has raised a $29.2M Series A and partners with gaming and betting operators. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing and newsroom presence only — no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface has been found.

providers.name: Caesars Entertainment
providers.description: Caesars Entertainment is the largest U.S. casino-entertainment company, operating over 50 gaming facilities, hotels, restaurants, and entertainment venues across the country and internationally. The company operates the Caesars Rewards loyalty program and offers gaming, hospitality, dining, entertainment, meetings and conventions, and retail experiences.

providers.name: 6 Waves
providers.description: 6waves is a global mobile game publisher founded in 2008 and headquartered in Hong Kong, with offices in China, Japan, and the United States. The company partners with independent game developers around the world to publish, localize, and operate social and mobile games, offering culturalization, product guidance, live operations, marketing, platform relationships, customer service and community management, technical support, quality assurance, and VIP management. 6waves is recognized as a pioneer of top-grossing mobile game publishing, particularly in the Japanese market, and is a portfolio company of Insight Partners.

providers.name: AlmostApps
providers.description: AlmostApps is a Sacramento, California sports-gaming studio founded in 2022 that builds free-to-play mobile entertainment experiences for sports fans, blending casual gameplay with real-life sports scores and stats. Its flagship product, Tailgate, is a free-to-play mobile sports entertainment app designed to enhance the game-day experience for casual sports enthusiasts. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Parade Ventures. AlmostApps is a consumer application company and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or API documentation; only a marketing site with Terms of Service and Privacy Policy is publicly available. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: AutoLotto
providers.description: AutoLotto, Inc. operates Lottery.com, a mobile platform that lets users in participating US states play official draw lottery games such as Powerball and Mega Millions from their phones, track tickets, view winning numbers, jackpot sizes and draw times, and collect winnings to a linked bank account. Beyond the consumer app, AutoLotto runs a business data-licensing offering that syndicates results and draw data for hundreds of lottery games worldwide to partner digital properties. AutoLotto is venture-backed (500 Global, Pantera Capital) and its parent trades publicly. As of this enrichment pass Lottery.com exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; data access is arranged through a manual "license our data" inquiry form rather than a programmatic surface.

providers.name: BigScreen
providers.description: Bigscreen is a social virtual-reality company founded in 2014 by Darshan Shankar. Its flagship Bigscreen app lets people watch movies, mirror their Windows PC desktop, play games, and hang out with friends inside shared virtual rooms across major VR platforms. In 2023 the company shipped the Bigscreen Beyond, an ultra-compact, custom-fit OLED PC-VR headset, followed by the Beyond 2 line. Bigscreen is a consumer VR hardware and software company backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors; it does not currently operate a public developer program or REST API. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: BIT ODD
providers.description: BIT ODD is a Helsinki-based mobile game studio founded in 2019 by former Supercell creative leads Lasse Louhento, Taneli Oksama, and Jani Lintunen. The studio hand-crafts casual mobile games driven by feeling and a sense of wonder rather than aggressive monetization, explicitly rejecting ad-spam and dark-pattern design. Backed by Index Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners, and Makers Fund across a EUR 5M seed and a EUR 17M round, BIT ODD is a consumer entertainment company with no public developer platform, API, or SDK surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead and carries only the artifacts that can be honestly probed from its public web presence (domain security, legal pages).

providers.name: Closing Theory Studios
providers.description: Closing Theory Studios, Inc. is an independent mobile game studio founded in 2023 and based in Austin, Texas, on a mission to bring the real world into games. Its debut title, Househunt (the officially licensed ZillowGoneWild game), lets the 70 million-plus people who browse Zillow for fun buy, guess prices on, renovate, flip, and manage real houses in a casual mobile experience aimed at "non-gamers." The studio was co-founded by Ankith Harathi and Nitin Rajinikanth and raised a $2.3M round led by a16z GAMES SPEEDRUN, with participation from Powerhouse Capital and angel Seth Sivak (founder of Proletariat, acquired by Blizzard). Closing Theory Studios ships consumer mobile games on iOS and Android and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: ELKROOM CO., LTD.
providers.description: ELKROOM CO., LTD. is a consumer mobile-gaming studio and 500 Global portfolio company behind the OXO product family. Its flagship OXO Game Launcher is an Android game launcher and optimization tool that organizes a player's games and automatically tracks play history, journals, monthly reports, rankings, and community activity, and has surpassed five million downloads on Google Play. The company also builds OXO Gameplay, an AI-powered gaming content and social platform for Android and iOS, and Stricer, a cloud-based AI video analysis and highlight-editing tool on the web. ELKROOM operates consumer applications rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its public identity, product surface, and legal/policy pages. Tagline: "You Chase Glory. We Make It Legendary."

providers.name: Everyrealm
providers.description: Everyrealm Inc. is a Web3 and metaverse company building virtual communities inside in-game worlds, positioned at the intersection of gaming, entertainment, and blockchain technology. Under the banner "Connecting what matters," Everyrealm develops immersive, gamified virtual worlds and experiences, partners with gaming platforms, and invests across the broader metaverse and digital-real-estate ecosystem. The company has raised venture funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Coinbase Ventures, Brevan Howard, Hashed, and other prominent investors. Everyrealm is a consumer- and community-facing operator rather than an API-first developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, or programmatic API surface. This entry was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile and has been enriched with public identity, legal, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Flickplay
providers.description: Flickplay, Inc. is a Web3 social and gaming company that turns character intellectual property into portable, interactive, and monetizable experiences across user-generated content, social platforms, and real-world retail activations. Its consumer iOS app combines character-based gameplay (blind boxes, spin games, leveling), AR video and GIF creation tools, AI character chat, iOS home-screen widgets, a quest system tying gameplay to e-commerce, and a Fandom Intelligence dashboard tracking fan identity, behavior, and spend. Flickplay is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of mid-2026 the company published a suspension notice, and it exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal — this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Gen.G
providers.description: Gen.G is a global esports organization founded in 2017 (originally KSV eSports) that connects the United States and Asia, operating from Los Angeles, Seoul, and Shanghai. It fields professional teams across League of Legends, Valorant, PUBG, Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League, Fortnite, Brawl Stars, Honor of Kings, Mobile Legends, NBA 2K, Overwatch, Rainbow Six Siege, and EA FC, and runs a youth esports academy program alongside merchandise and fan-engagement businesses. Backed by Canaan Partners among other investors, Gen.G was valued at roughly $250 million as of 2022. It is a consumer esports brand and merchandise operator with a Shopify-based storefront; it publishes no public developer API, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Good Job Games
providers.description: Good Job Games is a global mobile gaming company founded in 2017 that designs, develops, and operates puzzle and match-3 titles for iOS and Android, including Wonder Blast and Match Villains. The studio publishes its games through the Apple App Store and Google Play rather than a developer API program, and its public web surface is limited to its marketing site, games catalog, careers ("Life at Good Job Games") pages, and legal policies. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, SDK, documentation, or API reference was found during enrichment; the artifacts captured here reflect its domain security posture and public web properties.

providers.name: Grand Games
providers.description: Grand Games (Grand Games Oyun ve Yazılım) is an Istanbul-based hybrid-casual mobile game studio founded in early 2024 by Bekir Batuhan Çelebi, Mehmet Çalım, and Mustafa Fırtına, a team that previously built Zen Match at Moon Active. The studio develops genre-defining puzzle games for iOS and Android played by millions worldwide, including Magic Sort, Car Match, and Block Out, and has grown to six live titles with fivefold year-over-year revenue. It has raised roughly $103M across three rounds, most recently a $70M Series B led by Balderton Capital's Growth Fund in May 2026. Grand Games publishes consumer mobile games and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Mission Control Games
providers.description: Mission Control Games is a mobile game studio building casual puzzle games, co-founded by Kivanc Okutur (CEO) and Murat Gurel (CTO), veterans of the team behind Merge Dragons. Headquartered across London and Istanbul (legal entity Mission Control Games Yazilim Anonim Sirketi), the studio works in small teams to create new casual puzzle sub-genres through rapid iteration and AI-assisted development. It launched publicly in April 2026 alongside a $4M pre-seed round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Arcadia Gaming Partners and e2vc. The company operates a marketing website only and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable developer surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Mother Games
providers.description: Mother Games is a Brooklyn, New York consumer gaming studio backed by GV (Google Ventures). As of mid-2026 the company is pre-launch: it operates a public waitlist for its debut social title "Le Zoo" and runs a campus ambassador program from its Williamsburg mailbox address (223 Bedford Ave #200, Brooklyn, NY 11211). Mother Games does not currently expose any public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer platform surface — probes of the domain returned 404 for every /.well-known/, /llms.txt, /openapi.json, /api, /docs, and /developers path. This profile tracks the company identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead pending any future developer platform.

providers.name: PLAYSTUDIOS
providers.description: PLAYSTUDIOS, Inc. (Nasdaq: MYPS) is a developer and publisher of free-to-play casual and casino-style mobile and social games, including myVEGAS Slots, POP! Slots, MGM Slots Live, myKONAMI, Tetris Block Puzzle, Solitaire, Bingo, and Mahjong titles. Its differentiating platform, playAWARDS, is a loyalty rewards engine that lets players earn real-world rewards from brand partners across gaming, hospitality, dining, and entertainment. The company is headquartered in Las Vegas and went public in 2021 via a business combination with Acies Acquisition Corp. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a dcm-ventures portfolio company; PLAYSTUDIOS publishes consumer-facing games and corporate/investor properties but no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: SuperGaming
providers.description: SuperGaming is a Series B-funded game development studio building multiplayer games "for the next billion players" in emerging markets. Headquartered in Singapore with a studio in Pune, India, the company develops and operates titles including Indus (battle royale), Prime Rush, Prime Rush MENA, SHOWDOWN, MaskGun (110M+ installs), Tower Conquest, and Silly Royale. SuperGaming also runs SuperPlatform, a proprietary real-time multiplayer and live-ops engine that powers its own games and 15+ other titles, and offers publisher services such as co-development, LiveOps-as-a-service, localization, and user acquisition. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal for external developers; SuperPlatform is an internal engine offered through partnerships rather than a self-serve API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z.

providers.name: Yuga Labs
providers.description: Yuga Labs is a Web3 company and the creator of the Bored Ape Yacht Club (BAYC), Mutant Ape Yacht Club (MAYC), and the Otherside metaverse, along with related NFT collections and intellectual property. Backed by a16z, Bond Capital, GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners and SV Angel, the company operates in the crypto / NFT sector on the Ethereum blockchain. It does not publish a formal, documented public developer API program; its on-chain assets are accessed via Ethereum smart contracts and third-party marketplaces (OpenSea, Blur), and Otherside exposes the forthcoming Otherside Development Kit (ODK) for building within the metaverse. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with the available public identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: DraftKings
providers.description: DraftKings is a digital sports entertainment and gaming company that operates a leading daily fantasy sports platform, an online sportsbook, and an iGaming casino across regulated jurisdictions in North America. The company also runs DraftKings Marketplace for digital collectibles and offers business-to-business gaming technology. No publicly documented developer API or developer portal is currently exposed at draftkings.com; integrations are typically handled through licensed partner agreements rather than self-serve developer access.

providers.name: PokéAPI GraphQL
providers.description: GraphQL beta endpoint for PokéAPI providing Hasura-powered queries over the complete Pokémon database including species, moves, abilities, items, evolutions, and game version data.

providers.name: Scopely
providers.description: Scopely is a global, mobile-first interactive entertainment and video game company that develops and publishes some of the highest-grossing free-to-play titles, including Monopoly GO!, Stumble Guys, MARVEL Strike Force, Star Trek Fleet Command, WWE Champions, Scrabble GO, Yahtzee With Buddies and Wheel of Fortune. Headquartered in Culver City, California with studios worldwide, Scopely operates both internal Scopely Studios and external Partner Studios on a shared live-operations platform, and was acquired by Savvy Games Group in 2023. It maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source data, streaming and infrastructure tooling, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification or SDK surface for third-party integration.

providers.name: Surglasses Inc.
providers.description: Surglasses Inc. (SURGLASSES) is a medical technology manufacturer of augmented reality surgical guidance systems and medical education products. Its portfolio includes AR-guided surgical navigation for orthopedic, spine, and neurosurgery procedures (the Foresee-X AR surgical glasses), 3D computer surgical navigation and planning software, and the Asclepius AI Table and Virtual Dissection Table for anatomy, radiology, and histopathology education. Backed by 500 Global. The company operates as a B2B medical-device manufacturer and publishes no public developer, API, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Incite Interactive
providers.description: Incite Interactive is an AI-native gaming studio founded in 2023 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz's Speedrun program, building AI-powered emergent narrative games where the stories players tell matter more than the ones they are told. Its "Everything Story Engine" is an agentic game engine that lets anyone create AI characters and living-world scenarios, powering products such as Embark and Incite Worlds — a roleplaying sandbox of human and AI-driven characters. The founding team are veterans of Zynga, Roblox, and Manticore Games with deep expertise in language models, user-generated content, and live-game operations. There is no public developer API or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Wildcard
providers.description: Wildcard is a PvP collectible-card-based MOBA (multiplayer online battle arena) developed by Playful Studios and currently in Early Access on Steam. Players pick Champions, assemble decks of Summon creature cards, and compete in real-time strategic arena battles where deck-building matters as much as mechanical skill. The game ships collectible cosmetics (Wildpass, Flair, Wildfile) with a web3 angle — the Wildpass is a Polygon NFT collection tradeable on Magic Eden — and is backed as a portfolio company of the crypto venture firm Paradigm. Its backend gaming services are built on Beamable and Unreal Engine. No first-party public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal is published; this profile is a company/lead record in the API Evangelist network. Sector: gaming.

providers.name: Atmosplay
providers.description: Atmosplay was a mobile advertising technology company, founded in 2014 in Budapest, Hungary, that built interactive 3D "playable" ads and an ad-monetization platform for mobile game publishers. Its ATMIQ cloud gameplay engine let users try a game inside an ad without installing it, and its self-serve builder produced playable creatives for 3D and action games. Atmosplay shipped first-party mobile SDKs (Unity, iOS, Android) plus AdMob and MoPub mediation adapters for publishers to integrate interstitial, banner, and rewarded-video formats. Speedinvest led its Series A in 2016; the company was acquired by ZPLAY Information Technology on 2018-01-01. Its websites (atmosplay.com / atmosplay.net) are no longer operational; the surviving public developer surface is its GitHub organization of SDK and adapter repositories. This profile is maintained for network completeness as an acquired/inactive portfolio lead.

providers.name: E-Pal
providers.description: E-Pal is a gaming social platform with the tagline "Never Battle Alone" that connects gamers to find teammates, compete, and socialize around competitive and casual gaming experiences. Its mobile apps (iOS and Android) let users discover gaming companions ("ePals"), form squads, use voice chat, play minigames, and hang out in social spaces. Product surfaces include Games (finding great teammates for titles like League of Legends and Valorant), Chilling (social hangout spaces), and Custom personalized experiences, plus a tiered community of eStars, Legend ePals (professional-rank players), and E-Chat. E-Pal is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time; this profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched as an identity-only lead.

providers.name: Future Trash
providers.description: Future Trash is a Los Angeles-based independent, multidisciplinary creative game studio and the developer behind FOAD, a user-generated-content (UGC) native video game franchise. Founded around 2022, the team first built a vertical-slice MVP of FOAD in Unreal Engine 5 and released it in early access on Steam. After Epic Games launched Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN) in 2023, the studio pivoted to building FOAD experiences natively inside Fortnite's UGC ecosystem, spanning MOBA, tycoon, and combat modes, while planning to resume the standalone UE5 core game. Future Trash raised a $5M seed round in September 2024 led by TIRTA Ventures with participation from General Catalyst. This profile was surfaced from General Catalyst's portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; Future Trash is a game studio and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: L'Oréal
providers.description: L'Oréal is the world's largest cosmetics and beauty company, producing skincare, makeup, haircare, and fragrance products. The group operates a portfolio of over 35 brands, including Lancôme, Maybelline, Garnier, NYX Professional Makeup, Kérastase, La Roche-Posay, and Kiehl's, sold in over 150 countries. L'Oréal's primary developer surface is the ModiFace platform (a wholly owned subsidiary), which exposes an AR virtual try-on SDK and API for partner brands and retailers. L'Oréal Group itself does not operate a general-purpose corporate developer portal.

providers.name: ThatGameCompany
providers.description: ThatGameCompany is an American independent video game studio founded in 2006 by Jenova Chen and Kellee Santiago, known for emotionally driven, art-forward titles including Flow, Flower, Journey, and the free-to-play social adventure Sky: Children of the Light. The studio focuses on creating timeless interactive entertainment that inspires human connection across all ages. It publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a technology / gaming entity and records domain-security posture from live probes.

providers.name: One More Game
providers.description: One More Game is a fully remote game development studio founded by veterans behind titles such as Warcraft, Diablo, StarCraft, and Guild Wars. The team builds delightful, social online games designed to be played with friends, emphasizing fast iteration and a mission to help players have more fun. One More Game was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. The studio publishes a consumer gaming website, a company blog, careers listings, and a GitHub organization (PlayOneMoreGame) of game-development tooling and forks, but does not currently operate a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: MoonFrost
providers.description: MoonFrost is a cozy life-sim RPG developed by Oxalis Games Ltd., set in a world ravaged by constant meteor storms where players farm, fish, craft, and build their dream home. Positioned as a Web3 game, it is backed by crypto investor Pantera Capital and is available to wishlist on Steam and the Epic Games Store, with a community on Discord. As of this profile, MoonFrost publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or developer portal — it is a consumer game rather than an API provider, so this record is identity-only pending any future developer surface.

providers.name: Touchten
providers.description: Touchten (Touchten Pte. Ltd.) is an award-winning mobile game studio headquartered in Jakarta, Indonesia, and an early 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. Its casual games - including Piper's Pet Cafe, Royal Garden Tales, Dessert Chain, Warung Chain Go Food Express, and the Teka-Teki Saku (TTS) crossword series - are published on the App Store and Google Play, are played by millions worldwide, and cater especially to the underserved women gamers market in the US and Europe. Touchten won the Google Play Indonesia Games Contest and received the Forbes Indonesia Rising Global Stars Award. The company publishes no developer portal or public API surface.

providers.name: Community Gaming
providers.description: Community Gaming is a web3 esports and gaming platform where players earn cryptocurrency rewards by competing in tournaments and completing quests. Players link a Sequence wallet, collect keys from quests and matches to open loot boxes and giveaway tickets, and enter prize draws paid out in USDC. The platform also serves tournament organizers with hosting tools, sponsorships, and grants. Backed by Multicoin Capital, it publishes a public knowledge center for players and organizers but does not currently document a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs.

providers.name: Fifth Door
providers.description: Fifth Door is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed (Fall 2025) AI-native gaming startup founded by Amir Ghazvinian and Daniel Kan that lets anyone create, share, and play games simply by describing what they imagine, with no coding required. Its generative-AI platform turns natural-language prompts into playable, customizable games, aiming to collapse the time, cost, and technical complexity of traditional game development for players, creators, and studios. Backed by Felicis, the company runs a consumer web app and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: Raid Base
providers.description: Raid Base Inc. is a Los Angeles-based game development studio, founded in 2020, building an open-world, sandbox PvPvE game in an original IP where players and crews build reputations through farming, trading, building, fighting, and politics. The team draws from Riot Games, Valve, Blizzard, Microsoft, and Bungie, and the studio has raised roughly $34.4M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), BITKRAFT Ventures, Patron, F4 Fund, and Dreamhaven. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the studio publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Distance
providers.description: Distance (Distance Technologies) is a Helsinki-based frontier-tech company pioneering glasses-free extended reality (XR) built on computational optics and lightfield technology. Its systems turn transparent surfaces — vehicle windshields, aircraft canopies, and head-mounted visors — into intelligent heads-up displays without screens, overlays, or wearable glasses. Products include the Acuity visual-intelligence platform and Acuity OS for defense, the Field Operator HUD (FOH) head-mounted system in field trials across NATO countries, and panoramic lightfield HUDs for automotive ADAS and navigation. Distance is backed by GV (Google Ventures) and partners with defense, aerospace, and automotive organizations including Kia, Supacat, Galvion, Patria, and General Dynamics. The company publishes no public API or developer program; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Gardens
providers.description: Gardens (Gardens Interactive) is a distributed, remote-first video game studio founded in 2021 by veterans of Journey, What Remains of Edith Finch, Sky: Children of the Light, Blaseball, Dustforce, Guild Wars 2, and Firewatch. The studio builds lush, living worlds that bring players together to cultivate lasting friendships, and is developing an upcoming shared fantasy adventure — an ever-evolving online multiplayer sandbox set in a shapeshifting, unpredictable wilderness filled with mystery and magic, designed around meaningful moments shared between strangers. Co-founded by Chris Bell, Lexie Dostal, and Stephen Bell and based primarily out of Portland and Los Angeles, Gardens raised a $31.3M Series A co-led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. As a game studio, Gardens publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: GuildFi
providers.description: GuildFi was a Web3 gaming platform and guild that aggregated blockchain games, quests, achievements, and rewards into a single account layer, letting players discover games and earn across the play-to-earn ecosystem (native token GF). It was backed by Pantera Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Animoca Brands, and other crypto investors. In 2024 GuildFi rebranded and consolidated into Zentry (zentry.com), a self-described "Human-Agentic OS" spanning gaming (Radiant), a data layer (zData), an agent layer (zAI), and the ZENT token. The original guildfi.com domain is now defunct (expired TLS certificate, 404s) and GuildFi/Zentry publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or agent surface as of this enrichment pass. This record is a portfolio-lead stub retained for lineage; see x-successor for the live entity.

providers.name: Third Dimension AI
providers.description: Third Dimension AI is a spatial-generation company building high-fidelity 3D worlds and simulation for embodied AI, autonomy, robotics, gaming, and entertainment. Its core product, SuperSim, models the world across the full fidelity spectrum - from real-world reconstruction of scenes captured from sensor data to open-ended generative simulation - so autonomy teams can validate, train, and deploy AI systems and close the simulation-to-reality domain gap without hand-built 3D art. Founded by Tolga Kart (CEO) and Piotr Sokolski (CTO), with Oxford professor Christian Rupprecht as Chief Researcher, the team draws on experience from Wayve, Tesla, Google, Luma AI, Nvidia, Niantic, Amazon, and Unity. The company raised $7 million and is backed by Felicis. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; enrichment captured its identity and probed its domain security posture.

providers.name: Those Beyond
providers.description: Those Beyond is a fandom entertainment company that merges gaming and community into immersive, location-based and online experiences for fans, gamers, and creators. Built by the Cauldron Co studio and backed by Seedcamp, it runs interactive worlds and events tied to major fandoms (including Invincible- and SCP-branded experiences) alongside a Discord community. Its public surface is a consumer marketing site on Squarespace; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or /.well-known/ discovery documents.

providers.name: Rangers Protocol
providers.description: Rangers Protocol is an EVM-compatible Layer 1 blockchain (Chain ID 2025) built for Web3 games and metaverse applications, using a VRF+BLS consensus mechanism to handle high-frequency transactions and a heterogeneous relay chain for true cross-chain interoperability. It features a virtual-machine ("blockchain virtualization") design, an NFT protocol emphasizing data inheritance and reuse, an on-chain oracle, and the Grand Guard Safe security tooling. Its native gas token, RPG (Rangers Protocol Gas), is also issued as ERC20 on Ethereum and BEP20 on BNB Smart Chain. The developer surface is standard Ethereum JSON-RPC plus verification-node operations; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: YoloRekt
providers.description: YOLOrekt is a social, hyper-gamified DeFi prediction-markets dApp where users bid on the short-term future price of crypto assets such as ETH, BTC, and MATIC, or provide in-game liquidity to earn game fees and YOLO rewards. Built on the Polygon network for high transaction speed, negligible fees, and full EVM support, YOLOrekt is delivered as Ethereum and Polygon smart contracts (including a first-of-its-kind synced dual-token issuance across both chains) rather than a traditional REST/GraphQL API. Backed by Pantera Capital and surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a crypto portfolio company; the yolorekt.finance domain no longer resolves and the project appears dormant, with its surviving public surface being the YOLOrekt GitHub organization, community bug-bounty programs, and the YOLOrekt Medium publication.

providers.name: agavegames
providers.description: Agave Games is a mobile game publisher based in Istanbul, Turkey, founded in 2021 by Alper Oner, Burak Kar, and Ali Baran Terzioglu. The company specializes in casual puzzle games played by millions, with titles including Find the Cat, Wonder Link, What The Hex, Soda Match, and Art Block Puzzle across iOS and Android. Backed by Balderton Capital and Felix Capital (Series A, December 2024), Agave Games is a consumer-facing gaming company; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Balderton Capital portfolio company and enriched with a live domain-security probe and identity hygiene.

providers.name: BLAST
providers.description: BLAST is a Danish esports and gaming entertainment company headquartered in Copenhagen, founded in 2016. It produces and operates premier competitive gaming tournaments and leagues (notably Counter-Strike BLAST Premier) and runs the blast.tv streaming and fan-engagement platform, delivering live events, broadcasts, and interactive esports content to a global audience. Backed by Creandum, Heartcore, Maki.vc, and Vaekstfonden, BLAST was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company. No public developer API, portal, or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures verifiable identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Brain Jar Games
providers.description: Brain Jar Games is a fully-remote independent video game studio founded by AAA industry veterans who have shipped franchises including Mass Effect, Dragon Age, RIFT, and Call of Duty. The studio builds bold, vibrant, music-driven action games designed to be shared; its debut title, Dead as Disco, blends kinetic gunplay with rhythm-synced choreography. Brain Jar Games is backed by Menlo Ventures and Transcend, having raised $12.2M across seed funding, and operates a four-day, 32-hour work week with team members across North America, Europe, and Turkey. The company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks it as a venture-portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Drill Creative
providers.description: Drill Creative, Inc. is a US-based video game development startup founded in 2023 in Cary, North Carolina, and backed by a16z's Speedrun accelerator. The studio builds original, high-quality gameplay experiences for user-generated content (UGC) platforms, the coin-op / family-entertainment-center (FEC) market, and PC and console storefronts. Its early releases are built on Fortnite via Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN), including "Elimination Confirmed," a 16-player competitive first-person shooter, and "Robo Bash," an arcade-style four-player fighting game. Drill Creative is a games company rather than an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or technical documentation, so this profile carries company identity only and no API artifacts.

providers.name: Gen.G
providers.description: Gen.G is a global esports and gaming lifestyle organization founded in 2017, with headquarters in Seoul, South Korea and Los Angeles, California. Gen.G fields competitive teams across major titles including League of Legends (LCK), VALORANT, and other publisher-run leagues, and operates gaming lifestyle, content, and merchandise businesses. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Gen.G publishes no first-party developer API; its public digital surface is the geng.gg storefront, which runs on Shopify and exposes Shopify's Customer Account OpenID Connect authentication for shoppers.

providers.name: GlamSt
providers.description: GlamSt (GlamST LLC) builds customized virtual makeover and try-on solutions for beauty brands and retailers, combining augmented reality (AR), artificial intelligence, and machine learning to power virtual makeup and cosmetics try-on across mobile, web, and in-store experiences. Founded with offices in San Francisco, Montevideo (Uruguay), and Wilmington (Delaware), the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. GlamSt was acquired by Ulta Beauty in 2018 and integrated into Ulta's digital innovation team; it exposes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Pax Historia
providers.description: Pax Historia is an alternate-history sandbox game backed by Y Combinator, where players explore branching "what if" scenarios and reshape the course of history through open-ended, simulation-driven play. It is a consumer-facing game product reached at paxhistoria.co with a single "Get Started" entry point; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer platform, API, SDKs, documentation, pricing page, or other machine-readable API surface. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead surfaced from the Y Combinator portfolio and enriched here with verified identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Puzzlium
providers.description: Puzzlium is a mobile puzzle platform and social network built around the tagline "Play. Create. Compete." Founded in 2014 by veteran puzzle designers Serhiy Grabarchuk, Serhiy Grabarchuk Jr., Peter Grabarchuk, and Mehmet Murat Sevim, the iOS and Amazon Kindle app lets a community of hundreds of thousands of solvers and creators play, generate, publish, and compete with interactive puzzles. Based in San Jose, California and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), Puzzlium is a consumer application that does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Take Two
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO) is a leading developer, publisher, and marketer of interactive entertainment for consumers worldwide, headquartered in New York City. The company delivers its products principally through three wholly owned labels — Rockstar Games, 2K, and Zynga — spanning console, PC, and mobile platforms via physical retail, digital download, online platforms, and cloud streaming. Franchises include Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption, NBA 2K, Borderlands, and mobile titles such as Words With Friends and Toon Blast. Take-Two is a publicly traded interactive entertainment holding company; it does not publish a public developer API program, developer portal, or API documentation at the corporate level. This profile was surfaced as a general-catalyst job-board listing and carried into the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment found no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Xiudan (Showball)
providers.description: Shenzhen Xiudan Technology Co., Ltd. (深圳秀蛋科技有限公司) is the Chinese company behind Showball (秀蛋), a virtual social "meta" mobile app where users create avatars and socialize in virtual spaces, distributed through the iOS App Store and an Android download on xiudan.net. A Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company, Xiudan publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts as of July 2026 - this profile records the company identity and probe results for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Heyzap
providers.description: Heyzap was a mobile-game advertising, discovery, and monetization company. It began as a social game-discovery network and pivoted into a mobile ad mediation platform, offering iOS, Android, Unity, Cordova, and Adobe AIR/ANE SDKs that let game developers serve and mediate ads across networks such as AdMob, AppLovin, Vungle, Chartboost, AdColony, and Facebook Audience Network. Heyzap was acquired by Fyber (RNTS Media) in 2016 and its brand was later folded into Digital Turbine. Heyzap never published a public REST API; its developer surface was the mobile ad-mediation SDKs distributed via GitHub (github.com/Heyzap) and package registries. The heyzap.com domain is now parked/for-sale and the developer documentation site no longer resolves; this profile preserves the historical, first-party SDK artifacts that remain publicly available. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Placenote
providers.description: Placenote (Vertical AI Inc.) was a San Francisco company that built a cloud-hosted persistent augmented-reality toolkit — a "Persistent AR" SDK that let developers save, reload, and share ARKit/Unity spatial maps so digital content stays anchored to a physical location across sessions and devices. It shipped native client SDKs for iOS (Swift, via the PlacenoteSDK CocoaPod) and Unity, plus multiplayer AR samples such as PlaceInvaders and web mesh-viewing examples. The product was consumed as mobile SDKs backed by a cloud mapping/localization service rather than a public REST API, so no OpenAPI or web API surface was published. The company is now defunct: placenote.com no longer resolves to a live product (the domain is parked) and the docs/cloud service are offline. The Placenote GitHub organization and the published SDKs remain the only live, first-party developer surface, which is what this profile captures.

providers.name: Polyup
providers.description: Let'sMOD (formerly Polyup) is a Sunnyvale, California company founded in 2015 that builds a consumer platform where users aged 8 and up can play, modify, remix, and share short 3D microgames and AI-powered interactive memes. Originally a computational-thinking and math learning tool under the Polyup brand, the product has evolved into a generative-AI-driven microgame and viral-content community at letsmod.com. Let'sMOD is a 500 Global portfolio company. It exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal today; its public GitHub organization contains only internal CLI tooling and configuration. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched via live domain-security probing.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: Light & Wonder
providers.description: Light & Wonder is a leading cross-platform global games company that develops and distributes gaming content across land-based casinos, mobile platforms, and online channels. The company's portfolio includes titles such as Dancing Drums Prosperity, Rainbow Riches, and Gold Fish, and includes subsidiaries SciPlay (mobile social gaming) and Grover Gaming. Light & Wonder operates customer-facing support portals for both gaming and iGaming partners.

providers.name: Downjoy (当乐网)
providers.description: Downjoy (当乐网, d.cn) is a Chinese mobile game distribution and community platform operated by Beijing Downjoy Information Technology Co., Ltd (北京当乐信息技术有限公司). The site offers mobile game downloads, gaming news and original editorial content, game-related video, community features, and game rankings and recommendations. Downjoy also runs an open platform at open.d.cn where game publishers and developers register, create and submit games, integrate the Downjoy SDK, and manage launch and updates. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; enriched with verified public identity and infrastructure probes.

providers.name: Matchday
providers.description: Matchday is a consumer mobile platform for collecting officially licensed digital football (soccer) player cards and building a squad, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The product is a business-to-consumer collecting and squad-building experience delivered through its mobile apps and website at matchday.com. As of this enrichment pass, Matchday does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or documentation surface: probing api.matchday.com, docs.matchday.com, and developer.matchday.com returned no reachable developer hosts, and the marketing site is a single-page application. This profile therefore carries company identity plus a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts, and remains a lead to revisit if a public API surface is launched.

providers.name: Oculus VR
providers.description: Oculus VR is the pioneering virtual reality company founded in 2012 and acquired by Facebook (now Meta) in 2014. Its Rift, Go, and Quest headsets defined consumer VR, and the Oculus brand has since been folded into Meta Quest and Meta Horizon OS. The former developer.oculus.com and oculus.com properties now redirect to Meta's developer platform. There is no distinct public REST/OpenAPI surface; developers build against SDK-based tooling (Unity, Unreal Engine, native OpenXR, and the Meta Spatial SDK) rather than a hosted web API. Backed originally by a16z; consumer VR/AR hardware and platform.

providers.name: Psychonauts
providers.description: Psychonauts World Characters Information and PSI Powers

providers.name: Airborne Entertainment
providers.description: Airborne Entertainment was a Montreal, Quebec mobile entertainment company founded in 2000 that published and distributed premium mobile content and applications for carrier decks and early smartphones, including games, ringtones, ring-back tones, images, video and informational content, often under licensed consumer brands. The company raised a $22M round in July 2004 with participation from Insight Partners and Verizon, sold a majority stake to Japan's CYBIRD Co., Ltd. in 2005, was taken back by management in a 2008 buy-out, operated afterwards as Airborne Mobile, and was acquired by Bandsintown in October 2010. It no longer operates as an independent company: both airborneentertainment.com and airbornemobile.com are parked domain-sale listings, and the company never published a public developer portal, API, or SDK surface. This profile is retained as an API Evangelist network history record.

providers.name: Coolso
providers.description: Coolso develops wearable gesture-recognition technology. Using patented sensing that detects muscle-vibration signals processed through its own AI model, Coolso recognizes individual finger movements and strength levels with low-latency response, from a wrist-worn device or an ordinary smartwatch's accelerometer and gyroscope without dedicated hardware. Founded by Sheng-Kuei Hsu, Wei-Lin Lee, and Jack Wu and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the seed-stage company is backed by 500 Global and Alchemist Accelerator and targets AR/VR interaction, with potential expansion into medical rehabilitation and sports equipment. Coolso publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Createra
providers.description: Createra is a user-generated-content (UGC) gaming metaverse platform backed by Andreessen Horowitz, built by the Code Infinity team associated with the youth-coding company Codemao. The platform lets creators build and publish infinitely engaging 3D worlds and games directly in the browser, founded on the belief that creativity is a talent that everyone possesses. Its Box3 creation platform published a first-party JavaScript web SDK to npm as @box3/web-sdk. As of a July 2026 probe the createra.fun website returns no response over HTTP or HTTPS, no developer portal, documentation, API reference, OpenAPI definition, or /.well-known discovery surface could be located, and the npm SDK has not been republished since January 2023 — this profile therefore records Createra as a dormant company with no active public API surface.

providers.name: Metafy
providers.description: Metafy is a consumer marketplace for gaming coaching and mentorship, connecting players with expert coaches and professional gamers for personalized one-on-one lessons, VOD reviews, and guides across popular competitive titles. Metafy operates a consumer web platform at metafy.gg and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; the only machine-discoverable surface found was an RFC 9116 /.well-known/security.txt security contact. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures.

providers.name: MoonActive
providers.description: MoonActive is a mobile game developer and publisher best known for the casual titles Coin Master and Pet Master. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a consumer gaming company MoonActive publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; the enrichment pass captured its security and domain posture only (a published RFC 9116 security.txt with a security contact and disclosure page, plus probed TLS/SPF/DMARC).

providers.name: Singularity6
providers.description: Singularity 6 is a Los Angeles-based video game development studio founded in 2018 by a team of experienced developers, several of them Riot Games alumni, with the mission of forging alternate worlds that deepen players' lives. The studio is the developer and publisher of Palia, a free-to-play community simulation MMO where players build a cozy life, craft, farm, fish, and explore a shared social world with friends. Palia launched into open beta on PC and Nintendo Switch and has grown to millions of registered players. Singularity 6 was acquired by Daybreak Game Company in 2024. The company operates a consumer gaming business and does not publish a public developer API program; this profile documents the company's public web presence rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Take-Two Interactive Software
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. is a leading developer, publisher, and marketer of interactive entertainment. The company operates through its publishing labels: Rockstar Games (Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption), 2K (NBA 2K, Borderlands, Civilization, BioShock, Mafia), Private Division, and Zynga (mobile games). Headquartered in New York City, Take-Two is a Fortune 500 company with studios across North America, Europe, and Asia. No public developer API is currently available.

providers.name: Tamatem
providers.description: Tamatem is a Jordan-based mobile games publisher and platform focused on the Arabic-speaking MENA market. It localizes and publishes mobile games for Arab gamers and operates Tamatem Plus (tamatemplus.com), a consumer store for game vouchers, in-game items, and top-ups with a range of local payment options. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Tamatem publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface — it is a consumer-facing gaming and digital-goods business, so this profile carries identity and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: TrialPay
providers.description: TrialPay was an alternative-payments and offer-based advertising company founded in 2006 and based in Mountain View, California, backed by Battery Ventures among others. Its platform let merchants and game developers offer users a product for "free" in exchange for completing an advertiser-sponsored action (a purchase, trial, or signup), with the advertiser paying the merchant — monetizing users who would not otherwise pay. TrialPay shipped web, Android, and iOS SDKs plus offer-wall and monetization APIs (e.g. GetBuyCoinsInfo / GetBuyDirectInfo) widely used in social and mobile games. Visa acquired TrialPay in April 2015 and folded the technology into the Visa Commerce Network; TrialPay no longer operates as a standalone company and its public developer surface (help.trialpay.com, trialpay.com) is offline.

providers.name: Crater Studios
providers.description: Crater Studios is an AI-native game studio that builds core AI systems for game design, decision making, and live operations, trained on real player behavior in production environments. The company uses its own live game launches as production laboratories, shipping titles such as Dwarven Realms, Gravebound, and Doomspire on Steam while building agentic tooling around them - a GDD Maker that turns raw concepts into production-ready game design documents, a conversational decision engine wired to live telemetry, automated playtesting agents, content moderation, and localization. Crater publishes a set of playable browser prototypes on craterstudios.ai subdomains as proof that its design agents can produce working core loops. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Crater Studios publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specification - its AI systems are internal platform infrastructure rather than a developer product.

providers.name: Cryptoys
providers.description: Cryptoys is an Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) backed Web3 digital collectibles company that lets fans buy, own, and play with blockchain-based interactive toys featuring licensed characters from Disney and Star Wars alongside original IP. Products are sold as blind boxes containing randomized digital toys across multiple power tiers and rarity levels. The company has since rebranded and now operates its consumer experience as Digitoys at digitoys.io, while retaining its identity account service at auth.cryptoys.com. Cryptoys is a consumer-facing collectibles platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and identity surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Drop
providers.description: Drop (formerly Massdrop) is a consumer e-commerce brand operated by Corsair that sells limited-edition, community-driven products across mechanical keyboards, audiophile gear, and licensed gaming collaborations (Fallout, Cyberpunk 2077, The Witcher, Call of Duty and others). Founded in San Francisco and backed by Cowboy Ventures and other investors before its acquisition by Corsair, Drop runs a direct-to-consumer storefront at drop.com with a Zendesk-based support helpdesk. It is a retail brand with no public developer API program; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company in the network.

providers.name: EPAL INC.
providers.description: EPAL INC. operates E-Pal (epal.gg), a consumer gaming-companion and social marketplace platform that connects players who want teammates, coaches, or company for online play. Through its web and mobile apps, users book vetted "ePals" across titles such as League of Legends, Valorant, and Fortnite for co-play, chilling (social hangout) sessions, and custom experiences, with a tiered recognition system (eStars and Legend ePals) surfacing top community members. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; no public developer platform, API, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: forgame
providers.description: Forgame Holdings Limited (HKEX 00484) is a Hong Kong-listed technology holding company founded in 2009 and headquartered in Shenzhen, China. It operates across cloud/light gaming, fintech, electronic trade, and cloud storage. Its web and mobile game publishing platform 91wan, run by PRC entity Guangzhou Weidong Internet Technology Co., Ltd., has distributed over 100 web games and attracted more than 200 million registered players. In 2016 the group obtained an internet micro-lending (fintech) license in the PRC, and since 2019 has explored e-sports and virtual-reality games. Forgame is tracked by API Evangelist as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; no public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: International Game Technology
providers.description: International Game Technology (IGT) is a global gaming company that delivers entertaining and responsible gaming experiences across all gaming channels and regulated segments, including lottery, gaming machines, sports betting, and digital gaming. IGT does not currently offer a public developer API program; its technical resources are delivered through licensed B2B partner channels.

providers.name: Jetapult
providers.description: Jetapult is a capital and support firm focused on scaling mobile game studios, combining operator-first funding with hands-on systems for monetization, user acquisition, market expansion, and operational efficiency. Its GamePac AI toolset helps indie studios create, grow, and monetize their games. Jetapult is backed by Accel and operates as a partner-and-capital platform for gaming studios such as Holy Cow Studio and UMX Studio. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Jetapult does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Metatheory
providers.description: Metatheory, Inc. is an independent studio of builders that makes games and, through an AI-led software division, tools built for makers. The team describes itself as builders, dreamers and doers applying what they have learned making games to software, building in public and sharing what they learn. Metatheory has been surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Pantera Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the public site (metatheory.gg) is a single-page marketing site with no developer portal, documentation, API, OpenAPI, SDK, or public developer surface; the only public contact is support@metatheory.gg.

providers.name: Rovio
providers.description: Rovio Entertainment is a Finnish mobile games company best known for the Angry Birds franchise. Founded in 2003 and headquartered in Espoo, Finland, Rovio operates multiple game studios and became part of Sega in 2023. It is a consumer entertainment company; its public web presence covers games, careers, press, and support, and it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Theorycraft Games
providers.description: Theorycraft Games is an independent video game studio backed by a16z, best known for developing SUPERVIVE, a free-to-play hero shooter / MOBA-battle-royale hybrid. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer game and community presence but no public developer API, developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; the corporate site is in maintenance mode.

providers.name: Tripp
providers.description: TRIPP is a digital mental-wellness company whose consumer app delivers immersive, interactive meditation, breathwork and mood-management experiences across virtual-reality headsets (including Meta Quest and PlayStation VR) and mobile devices. It blends guided sessions, generative visuals, spatial audio and gamified "trips" to help people manage stress, focus, mood and sleep. Tripp is backed by Mayfield. As of this enrichment pass Tripp operates a consumer-facing application and an Intercom-powered help center but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; its web properties sit behind a bot-mitigation (captcha) wall, so no OpenAPI, llms.txt, or /.well-known discovery documents were retrievable.

providers.name: Unleashed Games
providers.description: Unleashed Games is an independent game studio founded by industry veterans (World of Warcraft, Medal of Honor, Monopoly Go!) and backed by a16z Speedrun, building socially-driven cooperative games. Its flagship title Haven is a cross-platform co-op RPG for families and friends spanning PC, Mac, console, and mobile, with procedurally generated maps, village building, and collaborative combat. The studio publishes no public developer platform or API surface today.

providers.name: Altera
providers.description: Altera is an applied AI research company founded in December 2023 by former MIT computational neuroscientist Robert Yang, building "digital human beings" — autonomous, collaborative, and socially intelligent AI agents. Its research began with multi-agent experiments in games such as Minecraft and Roblox (agents that can play alongside a person like a friend), and produced Project Sid, a large-scale AI-agent civilization powered by its PIANO architecture. The team is drawn from MIT EECS, the Stanford NLP Group, Google X, and Citadel. Altera raised a $2M pre-seed and a $9M seed (backers include a16z SPEEDRUN, Patron, First Spark Ventures, and Eric Schmidt) and has since rebranded to Fundamental Research Labs following a $33M Series A led by Prosus. Altera is a research organization and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or client SDKs; its only public developer surface is the altera-al GitHub organization (the project-sid research codebase).

providers.name: bash.gg
providers.description: bash.gg was a browser-based indie game marketplace built on Solana (founded by Kyle Zappitell, a former Xbox engineer) that let independent developers sell games directly in the browser without the ~30% platform commissions charged by Steam, Xbox, Apple, and PlayStation, with 10% royalties routed back to developers on resale. It entered the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead and was kept as a stub. Re-probed on 2026-07-20, the company remains defunct - the bash.gg domain is parked for sale on the GoDaddy/Afternic aftermarket (NS delegated to afternic.com, null MX, SPF "-all"), there is no live developer portal, API, or documentation, and the company GitHub organization (github.com/bash-gg) exists but publishes zero repositories. Wayback captures show the site only ever exposed Next.js/NextAuth internal routes (/api/auth/session), never a public developer API. No provider artifacts could be searched, generated, or derived. No fabrication was performed.

providers.name: Blue Vision Labs
